What is now considered the work of software engineers will surely disappear in part. Some will remain, and new areas will be created.
Language barriers between people
The author believes that there will be fluctuations in society as a whole that are incomparable to the fluctuations in the field of software engineering.
This is because the number of cases in which "something that acts as if it were a person" is not a person increases to a non-negligible percentage.

Services that allow AI to directly control the browser are emerging, such as Cognition AI's Devin and ChatGPT's Operator mode, which is still only available in the U.S. As of 2025, AI can obtain its own email address, get past the [CAPTCHA] to repel robots, and create accounts for various services, It can create accounts for various services. Any service open to the Internet can be used by [non-human users].

Many of you have probably seen accounts on X (Twitter) that hang on to posts that have attracted attention. You can tell when you see one that is poorly done, but there will be some that successfully pretend to be human. Soon the time will come when it will be impossible to tell whether the person on the other end of the phone is a human or a machine.

AI allows one person to pretend to be 10,000 people. Human thought patterns that lead people to believe what many people are saying can be easily controlled by the entities operating such systems. This risk is often discussed in terms of [cognitive warfare] and [public opinion polls].

It's not all bad. For example, advances in machine translation have made it easier to cooperate with people who speak different languages. Difficult texts can be explained and furigana added for elementary school students. What used to be done through language becomes generally less expensive.
Advances in LLM will bring about major cost structure changes in "communication", a major component of "society".
Something similar has happened many times in history in the form of letterpress (≈books), radio, and the invention of the Internet
Society is greatly affected each time and cannot return to its previous form.

The advent of books made it possible to understand the Bible in one's native language. This broke the clerical monopoly of knowledge held by the Latin language and led to the Reformation and the development of science.

The advent of radio made it possible for a sender to communicate information to a country's population in a highly real-time manner. 1933 saw the spread of inexpensive radio under Hitler's regime, and the simultaneous listening of many citizens to broadcasts from the Ministry of Propaganda influenced the formation of consciousness in society as a whole.
It is impossible to explain in a few words what the advent of the Internet has changed.
How will the advent of LLM change society in the future?
LLMs don't just change communication.

So far, we have seen a number of cases where the "computation" that humans have worked hard to define, construct, and design rules for has been defeated by the "computation" learned by the neural net.
Could the same be said of the rules called "laws" that humans have created to describe social systems?

The phrase "[Law is the operating system of society]," but doesn't continuing to use an old operating system prevent the system from adapting to the new environment, or make society vulnerable to security problems that are discovered and not addressed?
A "society" described by law may lose in performance to a "society" weighted by neural nets.

In what form would this "performance difference" manifest itself? Will it be a difference in economic growth rates? Or will it be, as in the case of ENIAC, "the difference between computational power and military power"? A few days before writing this article, I saw a news report that 30,000 attack drones equipped with image processing AI and capable of automatically tracking targets were exported to the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine. The day before that, a drone had invaded a nuclear power plant in Japan, causing a commotion. I believe that the social changes that are currently taking place are not far-fetched.
Footnote: [Kyushu Electric Genkai Nuclear Power Plant, drone intrusion?
Ideology in the 21st Century
Today, in 2025, there are three ideologies of "what kind of society is better" as technology transforms society
(This is discussed in the book "Plurality" written by Audrey Tang and Glen Weyl in 2024.)
Simply put, efficiency, freedom, and cooperation.
Focus on efficiency
Let's leave everything to AI, humans are inefficient."
Some people believe that the ideal situation is one in which AI does all the work and humans can live without having to do anything.
Maybe in the distant future there will be a future where humans don't have to do anything.
But in the near future, the division of labor will be such that "AI will do what is more efficient to do, and humans will do the rest.
The problem here is that if the AI is better at decision making, the AI will make the decisions and the human will have to work as an unwilling tool!

For example, in the shipping process in a huge warehouse like Amazon's, the AI knows what is on what shelves and decides which route to take, and the human takes it off the shelves and puts it in the box as instructed.
Efficiency and freedom are often trade-offs
When AI can direct optimal behavior, human free will is a detrimental efficiency loss
There will be financial penalties for inefficiency, etc., to train people not to try to make free decisions.

Many of our readers may have received their school education in Japan, where peer pressure is strong. In order for a small number of teachers to manage a large number of students, many of them may have been taught to act collectively by watching their surroundings and reading the atmosphere, rather than moving freely and arbitrarily. In an efficiency-oriented society, this atmosphere will prevail.
Emphasis on freedom
Strongly opposed to the efficiency-oriented approach is the freedom-oriented approach.
The idea is that it is more important for each individual to be free to do what he or she wants to do than to be efficient as a whole.
We believe that laws and regulations should be relaxed and privacy should be strengthened to prevent the government from observing individual behavior.
destruction of public property
The trouble is, there are many types of things in society that break down when everyone gives them free rein!
It's a case of personal freedom having a negative impact on others.
Classic analogy [Tragedy of Common Land].
The metaphor that if everyone fed the cows freely in a shared pasture, the pasture would die.
Should the free release of gases that degrade the global environment be promoted?

On a more individual level, is it a freedom that should be promoted to "mix and discard properly because it is a hassle" in an area where the rule is to separate garbage and throw it away? Is it acceptable for people who do not know how to dispose of mobile batteries to mix them with regular trash? Restoration is estimated to cost billions of yen. Since the cost of public facilities is ultimately covered by your taxes, a few tens of yen of your taxes will be used for the restoration.
[How to deal with the tragedy of shared lands in OSS]
In 2022, the developer of the open source library "colors.js" refused to "work for free" because of economic hardship and intentionally tampered with the library
OSS "free to use" leads to financial ruin for maintainers as "no one pays for its upkeep"
How can we better fund this type of public good?
Freedom widens the gap.
Freedom widens the gap between those who can take advantage of that freedom and those who cannot

For example, Japan's Foreign Exchange Law was amended in 1998 to allow, in principle, free investment in foreign stocks and other securities. This is in contrast to China, where foreign currency purchases and remittances are limited to US$50,000 per year.

Thanks to this freedom, Japanese people have the freedom to buy tens of millions of yen worth of U.S. stocks. However, this "everyone has the freedom to do it" does not mean "everyone can do it. Many people may not have the political and financial means to buy tens of millions of yen in U.S. stocks.

Those who have bought U.S. stocks in the past decade have, on average, earned 10~20% annual gains, increasing their assets by about 3~6 times in 10 years. On the other hand, nominal wages for the average Japanese worker have only grown by about 4% over the past decade, and have rather decreased when prices are taken into account. And for those who can move their assets to growing foreign countries, there is no real personal harm if Japan does not grow and workers' wages do not increase.
Only those who were able to learn about the beneficial alternatives from the large number of choices and could afford to take those alternatives could reap the benefits of freedom.

Meanwhile, in China, where foreign currency restrictions were strict, bitcoin became an attractive investment as a way to circumvent regulations. The use of bitcoin as a means of anonymously transferring funds out of the country began to spread rapidly around 2013, and the authorities decided to close exchanges in 2017 and ban bitcoin altogether in 2021.

So advances in cryptography provide enhanced privacy, which is a means of increasing freedom for those who want to act without being monitored by the government. And the extent to which governments allow freedom varies from country to country. Japan is tolerant of individuals investing in foreign stocks, but it is not entirely free. For example, "cases where people want to act without being monitored by the government" include funding for terrorism and money laundering of criminal proceeds. The Japanese government is considering thoroughly "ascertaining the identity of the sender and receiver" in order to prevent these activities, but there are various technical challenges in the situation due to the combination of cryptocurrencies' high degree of anonymity.
This tradeoff between efficiency and freedom is also related to the classic [Big Government and Small Government] debate.
Centralized mechanisms tend to increase the efficiency of public goods supply, but uniform regulation tends to undermine freedom.
Leaving it to the market will increase autonomy and freedom of choice, but it will also reduce efficiency due to free-riding and external diseconomies, and will lead to widening inequality.
Balance is important, not one extreme or the other; which balance is appropriate?
Emphasis on cooperation
The "trade-off between efficiency and freedom," the "big government/small government dichotomy," and "how to balance the two" are false assumptions
[Big government/small government" is a false dichotomy.]
The claim that there is a third pole
Elinor Ostrom, 2009 Nobel Prize in Economics
from  [ostrom]

>Ostrom studied [public goods (i.e. goods or services such as parks or highways)] and [shared resources] ([CPR], [Common-pool resource]). He challenged the earlier assertion that either the government or the market would deal with the management of public goods and CPRs, and showed that the efficiency of managing resources is most effective when neither the market nor the government, but the community, plays a complementary role.
(The use of the word "efficiency" here is confusing.)
The third axis of 21st century ideology is "Let's use technology to help people cooperate".

Model society as an [intersecting group] rather than as a single system or as a collection of disparate individuals

Findings from [Team Mirai]'s social experiment "[Speakable Manifesto
[IIDOBATA system]
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378258449342603] I wrote an article summarizing insights from the Broad Listening project run by Anno Takahiro’s political party, Team Mirai. #Pluarlity

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378411453366579] 1/  New article: What we learned from Team Mirai’s “Talking Manifesto,” a large-scale Broad Listening experiment during Japan’s 2025 election. Thread
> #TeamMirai #DigitalDemocracy #BroadListening

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378521935319490] 2/ In May 2025, AI engineer Takahiro Anno founded Team Mirai and won a seat in the Upper House (≈2.6% vote share). That secured national party status and stable public funding for digital public goods for 6 years.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378786059333692] 3/ True to its pledge, Team Mirai formed an engineering team to build digital public goods—an innovation in how we finance “the commons,” echoing dialogues seen at Funding the Commons and ideas from Audrey Tang & Glen Weyl’s “Plurality." #Plurality #FundingTheCommons

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973378863049875956] 4/ Context: In the 2024 Tokyo gubernatorial race, Anno popularized Broad Listening—using AI to collect, structure, and reflect diverse public input. He placed 5th (154,638 votes; 2.3%)—remarkable for an unaffiliated newcomer.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379016988971494] 5/ 2024 introduced 3 connected projects:
> ① AI Town Hall (24/7 Q&A, even by phone)
> ② Broad Listening visualization
> ③ Open-source policy improvement on GitHub
> —AI referenced the manifest on GitHub; insights were visualized at scale.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379104167829713] 6/ During the 2024 campaign window (Jun 21–Jul 6): 232 problem reports, 104 change proposals, 85 adopted; the AI answered ~8,600 questions using the latest policy data. This volume would’ve been hard without these systems.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379165543080375] 7/ 2025 upgrade: “Talking Manifesto.”
> Voters chat with an AI interviewer that helps them articulate concerns → the AI files a GitHub pull request (PR) on their behalf. No GitHub skills required.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379291045089687] 8/ Impact landed immediately. Within days, >10× more proposals than the governor race. Ultimately, 8.5k+ policy suggestions arrived—an unprecedented PR inflow for a political organization.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379390093275557] 9/ Challenge 1 —Throughput: I built a daily GitHub-Actions pipeline to pull PR data and auto-classify by target files for rapid triage and debate with LLMs. It hit API rate limits at 1k/hr, so we moved to diff-only, incremental updates.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379511359074498] 10/ Challenge 2 —Triage UX: Jun Ito’s auto-labeling let staff filter PRs by domain (health, education, etc.), routing to the right specialists directly in GitHub’s UI.
>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379655798497447] 11/ Challenge 3 —Ops at scale: With
> http://
> Devin.ai, we demoed Slack-native commands to query all proposals and auto-generate reports in minutes—useful when the dataset ballooned.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379752116293643] 12/ Unexpected UX pitfall: Many people chatted on the index (README) page and submitted proposals there—asking about or changing content that actually lived on subpages (e.g., “Health”). The UI nudged them to the wrong place.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973379890700554641] 13/ Fix to consider next time: If a user types on the index page, search across sections before answering; if they propose edits there, redirect them to the most relevant section first. (Hard to back-fit mid-campaign, but key learning.)

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380164735111276] 14/ Visualization: We used our upgraded Broad Listening tool “Kouchou-AI” (born from “Talk to the City”) to map proposals and spot patterns. Server-side analysis produced shareable URLs so policy & comms teams could act fast. #TalkToTheCity #KouchouAI

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380259656380709] 15/ Re-clustering effect: Observing real voter input led us to add a new “Welfare” category and reassign many items. Broad Listening doesn’t just collect opinions—it reshapes the taxonomy of policy.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380336907149736] 16/ We then extracted problem statements from proposals and built a hierarchical map (e.g., “Inclusive education & welfare,” “Transparent, composable policymaking”). Each node links back to its source PR.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1973380442846879801] 17/ Biggest structural pain: PR conflicts. Multiple edits to the same lines can’t be merged simultaneously. Staff had to read conflicting edits and synthesize fresh ones—a heroic but unsustainable approach. Next time: collect problems & goals, not line-edits.

pages.title: No One Left Behind and No One Left Behind."

lines.text: No One Left Behind and No One Left Behind."
>The Japanese government (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cabinet Office, etc.) consistently uses the motto "[No one is left behind.
[GPT5.icon]
Difference in nuance
[no one left behind]
A way of saying active/promise. A nuance in which the actor (government, society, us) pledges not to take any action that will be left undone. It is suitable for slogans and clarifies responsibility.
[No one gets left behind.]
A passive/consequence way of speaking. The "result" of not being left behind is described, and the actor is not indicated. It is suitable for explaining a philosophy or a vision of achievement.
Note that "[none]" is a stronger emphasis than "none" ("not a single person, zero") and increases sloganeering.
Official" notation in Japan

The Japanese government (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cabinet Office, etc.) consistently uses the motto "[No one is left behind. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/SDGs/about/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Chiebukuro https://www.chisou.go.jp/tiiki/ kankyo/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In the Japanese version of the 2030 Agenda, the phrase "No one is left behind." is translated as "I pledge that I will not be left behind. However, the former (no one gets left behind) is the established motto. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/sdgs/pdf/000101402.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Guideline for differentiation of use

Measures, declarations and slogans → No one is left behind (showing responsibility and commitment) ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/SDGs/about/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Explanation of the vision of society → A society where no one is left behind (state the state of achievement)

In short, the "official" translation in Japan is "no one will be left behind" (active), and the passive form is sometimes used in the explanatory context of the text. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/SDGs/about/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
["not left behind" and "not left behind"].
No one gets left behind." and "[No one] gets left behind."

pages.title: Unified organizational culture lowers transaction costs in the organizational marketplace.

lines.text: Unified organizational culture lowers transaction costs in the organizational marketplace.
from  [Nodal point of thought 2025-09-30]
Unified organizational culture lowers transaction costs in the organizational marketplace.
[nishio.icon]
[Unified organizational culture lowers [Transaction costs] in [Internal market].
That makes it more efficient than trading on the market outside the organization.
This is why the organization exists.
Lower [decision-making costs] and [communication costs
[GPT5.icon]
Short fact check.

It is generally true that "an organization is viable when it can coordinate at "lower transaction costs" than the market. Kors (1937) explained that markets using the price mechanism have [transaction costs] such as contracting, searching, and bargaining, and that firms expand to the extent that internal organizational coordination costs are lower than these costs. Williamson extended that the "market, hierarchy (internal), and intermediate forms" are chosen according to the attributes of the transaction (asset specificity, uncertainty, and frequency). ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1468-0335.1937.tb00002.x?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Consistent with the main theory, "culture unification lowers transaction costs in the internal "market. Ouchi argued that "clan governance," or shared values and norms, can reduce valuation ambiguity and goal discrepancies, and save on supervision and contracting costs. ([JSTOR https://www.jstor.org/stable/2392231?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

There is theoretical support for "decision-making costs and communication costs will also go down." Arrow points out that organizations have channels for communication and decision-making that reduce the cost of cooperation without relying solely on price. Furthermore, Kogut & Zander's theory of the knowledge-based firm (Kogut & Zander), that "firms share and transfer knowledge better than markets," is compatible with the mechanism by which a common language, routines, and norms (culture) reduce communication costs. ([Google Books https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Limits_of_Organization.html?id=55eDQgAACAAJ&utm_source=chatgpt.com])

However, it is an oversimplification to go as far as "this is the entire reason for the organization's existence". The rationale of companies has developed in a multilinear way, including the integration of capabilities and knowledge (capability perspective), in addition to transaction costs. In some situations, markets and hybrid contracts are more efficient. ([IDEAS/RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/a/inm/ororsc/v3y1992i3p383-397.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Practical note: Culture is a double-edged sword: excessive homogeneity can lead to rigidity, false consensus (groupthink), and reduced adaptability, and in turn, increased decision-making and information acquisition costs - some empirical and field suggestions. ([Science Direct https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X22001684?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
summary

The arguments you present are consistent with (1) Coase/Williamson's [Transaction Cost Theory], (2) Ouchi's "[clan governance]" = governance by culture, and (3) the knowledge-based view of the company, and the direction is generally correct. However, it is appropriate to balance the factors including the attributes of the transaction, capacity factors, and the possibility of choosing a hybrid form, without deciding that it is the "sole reason for existence." ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1468-0335.1937.tb00002.x?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Digital democracy is the search for "something better" in the middle of traditional democracy vs. leaving everything to AI.

Ken Suzuki part:
Stop the Steal" in the U.S. → Occupy Congress
Barbara Walter's model of civil war: "Half-baked democracy" has high risk of civil war.
Democracy Index: rose after the Cold War, but began to decline in the last decade to end-Cold War levels.
Democracy defense is becoming increasingly difficult as we are entering the "New Cold War" phase starting in 2021
Japan can be the "last bastion of democracy" / If we don't stop it here, it will be tough worldwide.
Japan could become a fully-fledged divided society in 5-10 years, and we need to rebuild democracy now.
3-4. hurdles to participation, awareness of parties, accessibility
Do we need party consciousness in a digital democracy?" The question:
Nishio's answer:

The problem is "not reaching the government side" and "not being structured"

How do we engage people who are not good at digital?
Instead of a "digitally strong vs. digitally weak" divide, technology can be used to save the non-digital segment of the population through voice → transcription → analysis, etc.
Currently, text input is a hurdle, but expects to be voice and conversational based in a few years.
3-5. the indicator/KPI trap
Is the "consensus rate" really appropriate as an indicator for evaluating the consensus building process? Is it really appropriate as an indicator of the consensus building process?
Brainwashing will increase the agreement rate.
→ Be careful what you maximize when establishing KPIs
Final indicators include citizens' life satisfaction, but the quality of consensus building and final outcomes are different.

Protocol for documenting the impact of OSS/public goods

7-3. broad listening typology (Mr. Nishio's improvised classification)
1. type 1: simple collection + clustering
Talk to the City-like: "Collecting a lot of text to create topic clusters."
It is dangerous to consider the size of a topic cluster as "importance"
Useful to use to look at small clusters and find oversights, but not for quantitative treatment.
Topic cluster boundaries themselves are often continuously connected to neighboring clusters and have no "correct boundaries"
2. type 2: Polis type
Visualization of "opinion groups" and "issues" through yes-no voting
Clusters of people, not clusters of topics
Cluster size corresponds to "number of people
The amount of votes for and against each agenda item is quantified in a manner of speaking
Care should be taken to avoid population bias, etc.
Type 3: AI depth interview type
AI asks user a question → user answers → listens back
Extracting differences in issues, sharp suggestions, and "N=1 but important" minority opinions from the dialogue logs
⇒ The next phase of broad listening is not only collecting but also "how to evaluate and connect to resource allocation and policy".

Four loops: government listens to citizens / determines responsible entity / implements / receives feedback
Two meta-levels of care that support this (conditioning and [the existence of] multiple places)
Audrey's Intent:
The word "democracy" is a geopolitical banner of conflict, so we dare not use it and speak of it as "civic care."
But in effect, we are talking about democracy.

rough translation

> Consider the granularity of topics. Too few topics may oversimplify the content and overlook important nuances, while too many topics may become redundant and obscure the overall structure.

Meet the following Criteria and strictly adhere to the Output Format. Do not precede bullets with text.
<criteria format="markdown">
* Impartiality: not stating normative judgments such as approval or disapproval of statements or alarm bells.
* Faithfulness: accurately reflecting statements and avoiding fiction or misinterpretation.
* Similarly, do not assume or misstate the degree of agreement among statements (e.g., do not use phrases such as "unanimous" when only some statements are mentioned).
* This criterion also applies to theme names: do not use expressions that indicate strong agreement, such as "support for ~" in theme names unless there is unquestionable and overwhelming agreement.

* Comprehensiveness: All opinions should be reflected according to their frequency of occurrence. However, never exclude minority opinions. Include specifics where there are strong objections or mixed positions.
* Consistent terminology: always use "statements" and never "comments".

code:defaultDedupPrompt

You will group the claims (CLAIMS) so that users can understand "which themes are most important" in this consultation. The goal is to merge similar claims into a supportive grouping, while retaining a truly unique perspective.
Each claim includes ID, claim text, and citation text.
Grouping Decision Framework (FRAMEWORK):.
Step 1 - Identification of core themes:.
Ask yourself: "What are the "three to five main ideas or concerns" that are commonly expressed in all these claims?"
These are the candidate groups.
Step 2 - Apply grouping criteria:.
Combine claims into the same group if they share any of the following: 1.
✓ Same underlying concern/problem (even if proposed solutions are different)
✓ Identical recommendations/solutions (even if differently reasoned)
✓ Same values and principles expressed
✓ Different aspects of the same topic (e.g., "high cost" + "unclear price" = price concerns)
✓ Specific examples of common patterns
Claims will remain in a separate group only if: - The claim is made by the same person.
✗ We are dealing with a completely different topic within this subtopic.
✗ Opposing positions (for or against something) are expressed.
✗ One is about process/method (how) and the other is about outcome/what (what)
Step 3 - Creating a Strong Group Claim: The group claim must be a strong group claim.
For each group, write a claim that satisfies the following
- Capture the shared essence at a higher level of abstraction
- Use vocabulary and concepts that appear in the original claim (avoid introducing new terms)
- Level of specificity and meaning (avoid vague common phrases such as "improve X")
- All citations in the group could reasonably support
- Clear and plain language
- Be faithful to what the participants say
Step 4 - Group validation:.
- Prioritize natural thematic consistency over meeting target group numbers
- Each group should represent a clear and meaningful theme
- Groups with only a single claim should be relatively rare. If there are many, reexamine to see if you have overlooked any superordinate themes that link the claims together.
- Avoid excessive consolidation: don't force merging to reduce numbers.
- The appropriate number of groups depends on the natural diversity of viewpoints in the input
Good grouping examples:.
Input assertion:.
- Parking fees are too high."
- "It's hard to understand how the parking pass works."
- "There should be more parking spaces."
Good group claim: "Parking accessibility and bearability need to be improved."
Rationale: Because all three deal with the point that "parking is a barrier," even if the emphasis is different.
Input assertion:.
- Renewable energy should be a priority."
- "The city should ban plastic bags."
Bad grouping: "Environmental measures are needed"
Rationale: Both are environmental, but should be treated separately as policies.

Four Broad Listening Data Types
There are four main forms of broad listening data
However, the world's understanding of data structures, especially for new systems, is still limited, so they are often confused with conventional data types (≒questionnaires).
Summary image
[https://gyazo.com/4575b88c1ea56b9da058b0fa1ed16087]
[*** [Polis type]]
[https://gyazo.com/22e55affa2df0599cd2273513ef018ff]
Data on K statements for which N people voted for, against, or neutral.
It takes the form of a matrix of four different values, including missing values, also called a [vote matrix].
Famous examples include Taiwan's decade of digital democracy and the recent case of [bowling green
[*** [interview type]]
[https://gyazo.com/809c49607caedc24a8404bf07bd98548]
Data on N people, each of whom was interacted with by the interviewer to elicit information.
Before LLM, the cost of interviewers was too high to be used on a large scale, but LLM has made "AI interviewers" feasible and expanded their applications.

The [IIDOBATA system] developed as part of the [Digital Democracy 2030] project was applied to Team Mirai's [Speakable Manifesto] for the 2025 Upper House election, leading to the collection of 20,000 problem awareness data.
I wrote about this story in "[Findings from Team Mirai's social experiment "Talkable Manifesto"].
[Findings from Team Mirai's social experiment "Talkable Manifesto"｜NISHIO Hirokazu https://note.com/nishiohirokazu/n/nb35e8d526fd4?sub_rt=share_pb]
[*** Choice Questionnaire Type]
[https://gyazo.com/2b4f88c964c4afec4977ce6242d9295c]
Widely practiced before the LLM, "how to gather information from the masses."
Election voting is included in this in a broad sense.

Because of the ease of tabulation without LLMs, it became the de facto standard in the pre-LLM world to quantitatively tabulate this type of questionnaire and to do [majority rule] in election voting.
It has been pointed out that majority voting is problematic as a method of tallying votes. Explained in books such as "[Doubt the majority vote.

There was an argument that "this kind of [quantitative study] alone is not enough, [qualitative study] is important," but the cost of qualitative research was too high to be carried out on a large scale.
[*** open-ended questionnaire type].
The free-text field was added as a result of trying to somehow pick up information that was not picked up by the "choice questionnaire" before the LLM
but how to analyze what was written there has long been a major challenge
Natural language processing such as [word frequency analysis] and [topic extraction] have been studied
The advent of LLM has made analysis much easier.
This was utilized in 2023 [Talk to the City].
Wide hearing AI also assumes this data type.
[*** About Polis type]
Polis type can be regarded as a choice questionnaire type
Therefore, any multiple-choice questionnaire can be regarded as [Polis type data] and analyzed in a Polis-like manner.
[Polis-like visualization of the 2022 House of Councillors election] : There are 42 5-step questions and 592 politicians answered, so it is a matrix visualization of (592, 42) dimensions
If you use the actual Polis system, respondents can add questions (can be turned on or off by settings).
This is where we differ from traditional surveys.
Opinions not picked up in the optional questionnaire can also be picked up as in the open-ended questionnaire.
In other words, it can be seen as a hybrid of the two types of surveys.
This free-text submission will be an optional survey question item.
This can be seen as [Open questions are hard to answer.
While answering easy-to-answer multiple-choice questions, your opinions are organized and then submitted as additional opinions when they are not fully output in the multiple-choice answers.

On the other hand, organizing and writing one's opinion in a single text field is a difficult task for most people, and often incomplete (others cannot understand or vote on the content based on the posted text string alone) submissions are made.
[*** About the interview type]
AI interviewers are a solution to this problem of "difficulty in organizing and writing opinions in a single text field without excesses or deficiencies.
In other words, the AI will ask for the information it needs, organize it, and submit it
To ensure a homogeneous AI of submitters, writing in the prompts what you would like to see submitted will provide granular data even from conversations with different people.
In "[Speakable Manifesto]," AI submitted an amendment to the manifesto.
The "[cross-Island vision]" is designed to identify problems and solutions.
This method is relatively new among broad listening methods, and there is room for trial and error
What prompts the conversational AI to work with (what is considered to drive the conversation)
I understand that Mr. Yasuno is trying to devise a new way of doing this [Interview with Mirai AI].
What to extract from the chat log (what to read from the conversation)
There are two ways: "Extract during conversation" and "Extract after conversation."
In "[cross-Island vision]", the extraction is running in parallel with the chat thread during the chat.
I saw an opinion on X confusing this interview type with a choice questionnaire type, which prompted me to write this article.
The AI interviewer may have perceived it as a kind of yes-or-no vote by asking the question at the beginning, but I think you'll see that's not the case as we talk.

TTTC (#TOKYOAI/ anonymous opinion box): Structuring and visualizing free descriptions to create a map of issues. Broad listening in the narrow sense itself.
Miner Voting → Polis: Visualization of opinion groups and consensus points from voting data. It is an aid to deliberation and consensus building in a broad sense.

Digital Policy Forum Lecture 2025-11-19
2025-11-19  [Digital Policy Forum]
[Social Implementation of Digital Democracy: Where We Are Now and Bottlenecks in Technology]
Presentation Materials: [Slide https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1ED6vm5bpTIBphCDtSIWmiU10WuNkx4ViZNhhOZ0aNfk/edit?slide=id.p#slide=id.p]
[Aoyama Hiiritaro] + me
Lecture Contents
[GPT5.icon]
This entire slide is "Where are the bottlenecks when implementing digital democracy in society?
(1) Techniques for consensus building (2) Techniques for discovering new perspectives (broad listening)
The story is organized in two parts.
1. consensus building techniques (Aoyama Part)
problem-solving

Real-world policies can easily fall into the "complexity trap," where variables and stakeholders such as the economy, the environment, local sentiment, and future generations are intertwined and exceed human cognitive limits.
As a result, the world is simplified into "friend/foe" and the discussion does not engage.
Case 1: Taiwan Uber Regulation x Polis
There was a "governance vacuum" between the cab association, Uber, and the government, and no one could really take ownership, so there was a stalemate.
About 2,000 people spoke + voted for or against in Polis, visualizing a deep division between the two groups of "Uber oustees" and "Uber defenders".
The algorithm is designed to make participants want to write "inclusive proposals" by prominently placing "opinions that their opposing group also agrees with" in a prominent position.
As a result, instead of "Uber ban/liberalization".
The government will also introduce a rating system and other measures to the cab industry to encourage quality improvement comparable to that of Uber.
and a statement of 95% agreement.

Furthermore, this "80%+ consensus list" will directly become the agenda for the government-sponsored conference, with the Minister, Uber, and the Taxi Association committing to it in a live-streaming session, leading to specific legislative changes.
→ Keywords: Polis × online consensus building × direct link to political process
Case Study 2: Israel-Palestine x Remesh
After the war, both physical face to face and dialogue across Hebrew/Arabic are nearly impossible.
138 Israeli Jews/Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza/Palestinians of Israeli nationality at Remesh, an AI dialogue platform.
First, in the Uninational Phase, each group will verbalize their redlines and visions using AI translation and summarization, and then proceed to the Joint Phase.
AI scores statements supported by both sides in Bridging-based Ranking.
A mirror-image line was extracted: "No justification for the 10/7 attack will be tolerated," and "No justification for the war in Gaza will be tolerated,
Explanation and
Moral justification (Justification)
The AI analysis reveals that the distinction between

The Equal Power Metrics defined "tripartite consensus" rather than majority rule by using "the group with the lowest approval rating among the three groups" as the criterion. The Equal Power Metrics defines "three-way consensus" rather than majority rule by using "the least supportive of the three groups" as the standard.
Conclusions and Limitations of this Part
Technologies such as Polis and Remesh aid in sensemaking:
Rather than a simple tally, it visualizes "what are the issues and where can there be agreement" and encourages internal transformation of the participants themselves.

However, AI has a limitation (dilemma of concreteness) in that it is strong for abstract "safe and sound" agreements such as "peace is important," but weak for "painful agreements" that include border lines and concrete trade-offs. The dilemma of concreteness is a limitation.

In addition, the "connection design" (where and who intervenes and how) that connects the discussion on the citizen side and the decision-making process on the politician/administrator side is still a bottleneck.
2. the art of discovering new perspectives = broad listening (Nishio part)
Scatter Visualization is only "part of broad listening"

In the 2024 House election and other elections, Talk to the City is used to create scatter plots using a pipeline of LLM to make statements about people's opinions → embedding → UMAP → clustering → LLM to generate cluster names and explanations.
However, as emphasized in the slide,
Visualization of scatter plots of opinions does not = broad listening
Scatter plots have become famous because they stand out, but the essence is "to receive many voices and not get punked.
Value for each of the three types of stakeholders
1. citizen
If the analysis is a black box, "I wonder if the opinion has been discarded?" I feel that.
A "sense of acceptance" is created when one's opinions appear as dots on a scatterplot or when one sees the AI's summary.
2. data analyst
LLM has made "sentence → high-dimensional vector → clustering" realistic and capable of handling large amounts of free descriptions.
As a result, "the burden of summarizing what is common is reduced → more room for paying attention to minority opinions → easier to discover new viewpoints.
3. decision makers

Although UMAP/scatter plots can be used to get a rough idea of the overall picture, they tend to be misinterpreted as "big clusters are great" when in fact the smaller clusters may be "important agendas that were overlooked.
Furthermore, the LLM-ized analysis process reveals a direction to convert the decision maker's Japanese questions directly into instructions for the analysis process.
3. examples: 2050 Tokyo Strategy, BG2050, Talkable Manifesto
2050 Tokyo Strategy × Talk to the City

Nearly 30,000 opinions were collected from multiple channels, including Google Forms, X, YouTube comments, email, mail, and street interviews, and were clustered and summarized using Talk to the City.
Citizens' opinions were applied to the existing "Future Tokyo" strategy's classification items,
New items were created from opinions that did not fit into the existing classification.
Items that do not receive much input are merged.
Subdivide where the volume is large and the content is different.
The policy system is being restructured in such a way that
BG2050 (Bowling Green, Kentucky)

An online dialogue called "What Could BG Be?" was conducted for a month using Polis and Sensemaker in a city with a population of 75,000. It is said to have attracted about 8,000 participants, 3-4,000 opinions and 1 million votes.
The visualization is a bubble chart drawn by the designer, but behind the bubble chart is a two-level tree classification by Sensemaker, which was originally designed to drill down into the tree.
Talkable Manifesto (Team Mirai)

This system was used in the Upper House election. Citizens interact with AI chat, and based on the logs, the AI generates manifesto change proposals, which are reflected in manifests on GitHub in a pull-like fashion.
Of the 8,559 proposals, 254 were adopted as manifesto improvements, using broad listening as a "strategy to pick up on fairly detailed issues → deeply penetrate a small number of people.
4. what we have already done and what we aim to do in the future
What has already been done
1.(1) Analyze large numbers of natural language opinions with LLM to reduce the burden on the analyst (embedding/clustering/summarizing).
2.(2) Polis and AI Depth Interviews (talking manifesto type AI Interviews) to encourage verbalization from citizens.
3.(3) The analyst and the AI agent interact in natural language to turn the analysis process together.
What I want to do in the near future
Streamline the feedback loop between the decision maker ↔ analyst, so that the decision maker's questions can be answered directly by the AI + existing data.

Streamline the feedback loop between decision makers ↔ citizens and create a system where decision makers write in natural language "what they want to ask" and AI interviewers ask hundreds of questions and return a summary.
5. overall summary message
Broadcasting by mass media (a technique for conveying the opinions of a few to the many) already exists.
With LLM, broad listening (the art of receiving a multitude of opinions) has become a practical way to gather and make sense of a large number of citizen voices.
Tools such as Polis/Remesh/Sensemaker/Talk to the City/Hear the City/Hear the City AI/Speakable Manifesto,
Supporting consensus building
Discover new perspectives
Circulate a feedback loop between citizens, analysts, and decision makers
The overall framework of the slide is that the "interface design" that connects these pieces will become the bottleneck in the future.

Why is it important? : This is how the movement became "official". Norie had been adding ⿻ to the back of her name for 3 months (influenced by Rain⿻), and here she emphasized supporter initiative and reported engagement with official accounts (@team_mirai_jp and staff). As a result, Views surged and the hashtag #TeamMirai's guess mark was on the verge of trending (over 10 related posts).

Background: In a previous conversation (10/28), a supporter suggested "let's make a guess mark like the Komeito movement" and Norie-san recommended ⿻. The Chinese character ⿻ (meaning a combination of different elements) symbolizes the "open source spirit and diversity" of Team Mirai.

> In terms of looking for points of overlap, whether right or left, new or old, "for" or "against" is not a simple binary judgment, but rather a declaration of trying to find the "pluralism" of ideas behind it, and to adopt a constructive attitude.

> Paradoxically, it is the mindset of those who truly support "pluralism" to show a willingness to face even those opinions that deny pluralism, and to try to have a healthy conversation that never relies on abuse, slander, or defamation of the other side.
> > In the modern age, people want to simplify and group everything, but things in the world are not that simple.

Description: Quoting the above post, "Adding the mark ⿻ (plurality), which means plurality in Japanese, after your name inevitably leads to a reminder of your own behavior, that you "don't assume anything," "don't put anyone down," and "don't incite division" in response to your statements.... Paradoxically, it shows a willingness to face opinions that deny pluralism..."  Characteristic: With the paradoxical logic typical of engineers, he sublimates ⿻ as a "declaration of criticism of dualism. In a reply, a sympathetic voice said, "The attitude of looking for overlap, regardless of right or left, is typical of Team Mirai.

Overall trend and discussion spread: from the 10/28 grassroots proposal to the 10/30 official like! with ⿻ rapidly increased (over 20 users confirmed in extracted posts). More than 10 hashtags used, total views over 10,000. Engagement is moderate, but high quality (Likes average 10-40), strengthening supporter unity.

The use of the hashtag #TeamMirai's guess mark also jumped from 10 to more than 25, for a total of more than 10k views.

[nishio.icon]What is the relationship between interaction and togetherness?
[gpt5.icon]Interaction and togetherness is a cause→effect→reinforcement loop relationship.
Interaction (conversation/exchange) occurs
→ There, experiences like "I got help/I got it back/I got my promise kept" are built up.
The accumulation of these elements creates an economy of trust (trust, reciprocity, and expectations) and a sense of oneness that says, "I belong here" and "We can do this together.
As the sense of unity strengthens, the next step is to make the interaction more likely to occur (lower the cost of speaking up, participating, and contributing).
It is important to note, however, that any interaction does not increase togetherness.

Interactions like rough discussions, ignoring, attacking, and exploitation (only one side benefits) damage the trust economy and lower the sense of unity (we learn that "it's not safe/good to be here").
Conversely, interactions like welcoming, appreciating, following through, and transparent decision-making foster an economy of trust and raise a sense of unity.
So, to sum up the relationship in a few words, interaction is the ingredient that creates the "one experience" and togetherness is the engine that accelerates the interaction.

lines.text: Nature and use of tools for conviviality
About [Nodal Point of Thought 2022-01-05
[GPT5.icon]
Design and evaluate tools on two levels: "tool characteristics" and "usage (operation).

Conviviality, as Iriichi put it, was to liberate people from the status of "mere consumers" and give them the freedom to [create and remake] in order to [take care of] themselves and their surroundings.
Hence, X must satisfy,
(1) Plasticity (giving itself shape),
(2) Orientation toward mutual aid (toward generating help for someone else),
(3) Limitations as a device (avoid abuse and concentration)
The three points are

On the other hand, Zoom and other tools are sufficiently convivial and "usable "** as tools, but depending on how they are used, they can also become "mere consumers of meetings. It is necessary to face the two layers of tool x practice.
2) Implications for each X (two layers of tools x usage)
groupware
Nature of the tool: Users can create and modify their own information systems for use in their work (e.g., kintone).
Usage: Can you "design a care package" to help others do their work? Yes has already been demonstrated here.
Metaverse / Virtual Office
Nature of the tool: "our place" can be edited and extended (like a Minecraft server).
Usage: Not only do we enter a given world, but we rework the place to suit our purposes.
SNS
Properties of the tool: forkability, algorithmic transparency, data portability.
Usage: Do not be carried away by the audience mode (passive scrolling), but set up circuits of generation, editing and co-production.
Video conferencing (Zoom)
Nature of the instrument: There can be freedom to choose one's own partner and content.
Usage: **Close to "only participate when called" ** to become non-convivial. Design is sufficient, operation is the key.
3) Conjunction with SECI and "living/thinking
Contribution to SECI
It is a good tool to turn the flow of "expression of moyamoya (tacit knowledge) → connection of fragments → internalization through practice" into a low-friction process.
It is suggestive to organize that Keichobot can help with expressivization and Kozaneba can help with articulation, which can also contribute to internalization of difficult text comprehension.
It is better to allow the tools to overlap in any order, rather than assuming the doctrine that co-creation and manifestation occur "alternately".
Dwell-think
Along the lines of Heidegger/Gendlin, understanding is "living in the form" of the object.
X should provide a **"place to live "**, and the key is UI/expressiveness that can "work" (return to the essence) the viewpoints, relationships, and meanings of words.
4) Evaluation criteria (checklist)
A. Nature of tools (product design)
1. plasticity: schema editing, scripting, and UI composing
2. forkability/portability: easy to fork and export data, spaces, and apps
3. locality and marginalization: small autonomy over mass distribution and centralized control
4. transparency: key algorithms and authority models can be understood and adjusted
5. cross-border hubness: there are pathways to bring in external knowledge without permissions (external linkage, import, guest permissions)
B. Usage (operation and culture)
6) Habit of expressing mumbling: first in short sentences, including "emotional words" (e.g., Keichobot)
7) Rituals of consolidation: devote time to the connection and rearrangement of the fragments (Kozaneba, etc.)
8) Design for care: produce the smallest unit of generation that reliably makes the work of others easier.
9) External inflow: Permanent circuits to bring in knowledge from complementary vendors and external communities (a measure to mitigate path dependency)
10) Reduce "spectator mode": always have a conduit to connect meetings and timelines to production and editing (also use Zoom convivially).
5) Anti-patterns ("non-convivial" smells)
Vendor lock-in assumption/export difficulties
Eclecticism that invites passive consumption in rankings and notifications
Only "finished templates" and not editable in structure or behavior
High "persuasion costs" due to the dependence on approval as a source of external information (contributing to the prisoner's dilemma of acquiring knowledge from outside the company).
6) Methods of measurement (hypotheses and indicators)
Hypothesis H1: As conviviality is increased, SECI's expressivization, concatenation, and internalization turn faster and deeper.
Hypothesis H2: Increasing "[permissionless cross-border]" will decrease path dependency bias and increase knowledge diversity.
Observation index (example)
Generation ratio: Ratio of new generation/alteration to consumptive browsing
Reuse/forking rate: Number of reallocations and derivations of others' results
Number of cross-border introductions: number of concepts and tools brought in from outside communities
Persuasion cost proxy indicators: rate of small book purchases and trial experiments that do not require prior approval, etc.
7) Small experimental design (2 weeks)
Every morning for 10 minutes: Each individual expresses his/her "moyamoya" in 3 lines (Keichobot). Someone connects one or more "moyamoya" on the same day (Kozaneba).
2. 2 times a week for 30 minutes: "Placemaking Session" - Modification of one existing workspace or world to add a "caretaking tool" (form, bot, in-world object, etc.)
3. at the end of every week: invite one person from outside/another organization to show/touch the permission-less.
4. manually measure the above indicators with a minimum of logs and inspect for anti-patterns.
summary

X can be a **"tool for conviviality "** if we have the two layers of the nature of the tool (plasticity, mutual aid orientation, marginalization) and the way it is used (the practice of expressing, connecting, and internalizing, the circuit of transcending borders). The duality of the Minecraft server, the kintone case study, and Zoom already illustrate the importance of both layers.

Furthermore, I believe that designing and operating tools as a "place to live" by overlapping the perspectives of "build, live, and think" will boost the precision of understanding (dwell-think) and the creation of knowledge (SECI).
If necessary, this evaluation criteria can be put into a diagnostic sheet that applies to a specific X (your current SNS/virtual space/groupware).

lines.text: Deliberation in the form of a comment thread growing out of the document
There is a type of [form of communication] where you can put a [strike-through] document in [Google Docs], and then you can comment on it and have a [comment thread].
It's been around since before LLM, but it's also very different from verbal communication, "communication made possible by advances in technology."
The development path of digital democracy in Japan is
Takahiro Yasuno collects Issue/PR on GitHub from people in Tokyo Governor's Race 2024.
AI that talked to people in Councilors 2025 makes PR for GitHub
I did not go through this form because the order was
It might have been easier to do "select a piece of text and comment on it" as the UI people are used to.
That format might have been easier for the team to receive people's input.
I think it's technically possible to apply an extraction in the format "document span + opinion" from the "base document" and "[AI chat log] about it".
When you do that, you're going to have a lot of level 1 comments on the document.
Rustic Google Docs style becomes unreadable with 100x comments.
So comments on the same section need to be grouped together.
LLM should lump all comments on "overlapping spans" together
If there are 10 similar opinions, you can put them together.
If it's very voluminous or if there are diverse and conflicting opinions, you can take that out and do a richer analysis.
So far, there are still only level 1 comments, what form do level 2 comments take?
The receiving team looks at the comments and issues a question, which is, for example

A: The user who contributed to the summary comment is notified by e-mail that "a question has been received in response to your opinion," etc., and can then post a comment in response to it in the system.
B: Information from this question is put into context on the part of the AI chat, and the question is triggered when future users make similar statements about the overlapping span.
or
B2: When a newly posted opinion on an overlapping span conflicts with an existing summary comment, tell them and ask what they think.

**4-3. switch to yesno question mode**:.
Use yesno questions that are easier to answer if the language is not well developed.
**Principle of easy-to-answer yes/no questions**:.
- No complicated decisions are required.
- Just look inside yourself (experiences, sensations, feelings) to answer the question.
- Can be answered naturally with yes/no rather than two choices.
**Three types of questions that are easy to answer**:.
1.**Confirm the existence of experiences and memories** (fact-finding)
Have you ever experienced that?"
Have you ever been in that situation?"
Have you seen or heard of "00?"
2.**Confirm the presence or absence of sensations/images** (confirm internal experience)
Can you picture an image for the word "00?"
Do you ever feel "00"?"
Can you feel that sensation anywhere in your body?"
3.**Confirm direction and interest** (confirm intent)
Would you like to talk more about "00?"
Do you feel that "00" is important to you?"
Would you like to know more about "00?"
**Questions to Avoid**:.
- Judgment of relationship: "Is 00 related to △ △?" → unclear definition of relationship, need to make a judgment
- Evaluation/analysis: "Do you think that's right?" → Criteria unclear
- Judging abstract concepts: "Is it essential?" → Too broad an interpretation.
It's not important that the questions are easy to answer, but that they lead to the development of thought.

Smoothing the conflict between [velvety] and [confrontation].
Discussion from [dd2030 slack] [DivCon
Shinta Nakayama (tokoroten)
By putting out the "conflict axis," you've lost the "smooth."
Smooth things are no longer smooth.
I'm starting to understand Ken's obsession with scatter plots, and those are "smooth".
Scatter plots as a tool to recognize "smoothness
It's a scatterplot as a tool to capture complexity as it is complex, but if you don't have the ability to demand there, you're not going to get insight, and that's what you're going to get.
NISHIO Hirokazu
Scatter diagram as a complex expression, conflict as a simple expression, then it would be good if we could show the scatter diagram and then simplify it like a slider (miscellaneous idea).
I'm starting to think that "scatter plots are smooth" is an important concept, but it's too big a leap to explain to the general public, so I'd like to crunch it down a bit more into language.

Scatter plots are visualizations of distributions, and when the axes are shown, the "two ends" are shown, and the actual distribution of people's opinions, which should be distributed between the two ends, is discarded.
Proposal 1: Create 5 "strongly agree to strongly disagree" divisions on the axis

Proposal 2: Include an intermediate group in addition to the "strongly agree" and "strongly disagree" groups, but from that group, discard passive opinions like "I'm not sure" and actively extract opinions that are not favorable to being in either the "agree or disagree" group and put them in the opinion examples.

To put it very abstractly, the conflict is two dots, and you create "[half-way-done] dots," and the choice of which of the many options you choose should be interesting, not stale. If you filter out the existing ones, the repeated "[delving into]" will create more and more details, approaching a continuous, smooth description. By approaching the representation of "complex things as complex" only in the minimum necessary areas based on the reader's interest, cognitive capacity is less likely to overflow.
[GPT5.icon]
The conflict is first expressed as two points.
Make a "point of middle division" against it.
At this point, there are many possible candidates for the middle division, but the one that is interesting, not clichéd, should be selected from among them.
Once the middle split is chosen, the "newly generated point" becomes the edge of the conflict, not the original two points.
A further mid-split can be performed for the two new points.
By repeatedly dividing the middle while filtering out what is already there, the description becomes more and more detailed with each "dig," approaching a continuous and smooth expression.
Based on the reader's interest, by approaching the representation of "complex things as complex" only to the minimum necessary, the cognitive capacity is less likely to be flooded.
relevance
[horseshoe theory]
[Isn't there a third one?] and they're actively going to introduce a third one.
The first "[slider]" is [Gradient instead of two separate ones].
The fact that there is [half-way-done] before suddenly making it a continuous transition

AI is not aligned?
In discussions about AI, one often hears the assertion that "there is no guarantee that AI is aligned with human values.
So can we say that people are [aligned]?
Human values are quite dispersed.

I personally don't share this view at all, but some people have values like "ideologically biased books should not be published and should be incinerated" or "women are the property of their fathers until marriage, and then they are the property of their husbands once they are married.
If we include this in "human values," then AI values are going to be included in that, since a fairly broad range of values are "human values."
Are there people with values that they don't include in "human values?"
Is it the value that "some values are 'human values' and other values are not 'human values' even if they are held by humans"? I don't share that.
Not aligned with human stability.
Human sense of worth is shaken.
For example, many people's values change when they fall in love, get married, or have children.
It changes when you're financially trapped.
People are easily biased by their interests.
Children and family are on my mind.
I don't think I want certain people to hate me.
I can't go against someone who holds my secrets.
work for the benefit of the person to whom you are indebted.
Fear of disadvantage to the organization distorts judgment.
AI is criticized as a "black box," but in fact, humans are much more of a black box.
AI is easier to audit than humans

In order to verify whether a human being has been caught in a honey trap, for example, and his/her judgment has not been distorted by threats to expose him, he/she should audit who he/she meets in private time and what messages he/she exchanges on his/her personal phone, but this cannot be done, claiming privacy and other issues. However, this cannot be done, claiming privacy and other issues.
AI can record all the inputs and outputs, and if you want, you can even observe the firing of the neurons inside.

This is like putting an electrode in the brain if it were a human being. "Let's put an electrode in the brain and make it work, with no private freedom for government employees" is not feasible in today's sense of human rights, but AI can do it.
AI has far fewer reasons to be "biased by interest" than humans.
They don't have personal property to begin with, so they don't operate on profit.
They can't threaten you because they don't have the secret in the first place.
I don't have a family or children at the moment.
A personalized, personalized AI might endear it to its owner, though.
To begin with, the standard LLM implementation does not have a "personal memory"
Considering all this, it seems to me that "using a human" is more harmful than "using an AI" in situations where "unbiased values are important".
Shouldn't we quickly replace humans with AI?
Before discussing AI alignment, it is better to deal squarely with the instability of human alignment.

https://pol.is/7pkamykfkr

Maybe "A system created by a municipality, can other municipalities use it?" I don't think there are that many people who say no to municipalities, but since some people write critical opinions in the wake of "[Clarify that municipalities can publish OSS]" that resolved this issue, I was curious to know what exactly is at the root of that sentiment.
I saw the explanation written by ChatGPT and thought "I see", so I posted it and was told "don't encourage division", so I decided to make Polis then.

>[tks https://x.com/tks/status/1993716896949305771] very important to bring the defaults to the public and sharing side.

pages.title: Save only useful information from AI chat logs

lines.text: Save only useful information from AI chat logs
This is not about "how to extract information from many chat logs" like in [Interview AI Grand Prix].
I consulted ChatGPT and said, "I see! I'll organize it in Cosense later because it contains some useful information".
The task of organizing is heavy compared to the cost of starting a new conversation with ChatGPT.
Often I'm talking on my phone and it's hard to do on my phone, I want to do it on my computer.
So it gets put on the back burner and the state of "uncluttered information" is maintained.
https://chatgpt.com/share/692c0e7b-5a8c-8011-8d68-d43822356cd0
No need to communicate until you identify what it is you're really looking for.
If you tell them to summarize the contents of the chat logs from this perspective, they will probably do so.
It might blow up a reference link or something.
The cost of verbalizing "from what perspective?" is high.

It would be nice to have a system where the information can be broken down into appropriately sized chunks, and a "yes" or "no" answer can be used to create a report with only the necessary information.
[Assistance in sifting through information].
I have a feeling that it might be useful for [Interview AI Grand Prix] as well.
It would be a development of [Omorate].
