pages.title: Reflections on the Digital Democracy Boom (Extended Questions)

lines.text: Reflections on the Digital Democracy Boom (Extended Questions)
I didn't pick up a lot of Slido's questions, so after the fact, I'll plug the entire list of questions into ChatGPT 5.1 and let it answer them, then I'll read them and comment on what I thought.
https://chatgpt.com/share/692c1958-1570-8011-a809-cf937529de16
[GPT5.icon]
This is the question you gathered at the event.
For the time being, we will add a "short, easy-to-use answer plan" to all of them.
(I am conscious of the tone that can be just barely usable even if it is copied and pasted directly into handouts or notes.)
Q1. "Democracy=Developing Technology" and "Consensus Indicators and Rankings?"
He sees democracy not as a "finished system" but as a technology that is still developing,
Not just turnout and satisfaction.
How seriously was the minority opinion taken?"
How many changed their positions after the debate?"
The time and cost of consensus-building."
and others can be designed as indicators.

Once that is standardized, I think we can create a leader board that says, "Which method worked better when measured by this rule? However, since the indicator itself is political, it is necessary to make the assumption that we will continue to openly discuss "what is considered goodness.
[nishio.icon]

This was a question that I picked up on at the last minute locally, but at the time I mistakenly said that the KPI would be the consensus rate, and that that was a false KPI setting because it would also be raised by brainwashing, etc.
AI's answer [" "How many people changed their position after the discussion?"] is pretty dicey.
The question text says "a measure of the quality of the consensus building process," which is an important distinction.
An "indicator to measure the quality of the consensus building process" is a different indicator from "whether the consensus building rate is high or not.
What would be the indicators to measure the goodness of the consensus building process?
For example, I think it would be important to increase "the percentage of people who feel that their opinions are reflected in the conclusions".
Q2. is China's authoritarian regime "post-democratic"? From an Efficiency Perspective

There are certainly phases in which authoritarian regimes appear to be more efficient than democracies when looking only at short-term "speed of decision-making" or "speed of infrastructure development.
On the other hand.
Cost of Correcting Erroneous Decisions
Risks from information concealment (pandemic, environmental, financial, etc.)
Instability during power succession
When "long-term efficiency" is evaluated, it is not necessarily superior.

I rather see this as a "transitional period in which each regime is experimenting with governance using digital technology. I think we should have a sense of urgency that if the democratic side fails to update itself to technology, the gap will widen further.
[nishio.icon]
You make an important point about the "instability in power succession" aspect.

Putin's invasion of Ukraine at this time seems like 73 year old Putin is concerned about his political life span OR biological life span, and the fact that China seems to be getting more aggressive in annexing Taiwan may be 72 year old Xi Jinping thinking the same thing.
Q3. as broad listening advances, will AI facilitate public communication?
I think there is a fairly high probability that "it will happen".
+1[nishio.icon]
However, the image is not "AI replacing humans,
Summarize and structure large numbers of opinions
Organize the issues for each position and
Highlight minority issues so that they are not overlooked.
The AI is in charge of the "preparation of the discussion.
Ultimately, people need to be responsible for making value judgments and prioritization decisions.
Q4.  [What kind of technology is effective for living in a complex world with complexity?]
I think the key is not "simplifying the world" but rather technology that "makes complexity manageable." For example.
Visualization tools to show multiple perspectives side by side (maps, graphs, diagrams of conflict structures)
Showing side-by-side opinions of people with values near and far from yours Recommendations
Traceability tools to ensure that the process of decision making is well documented
Such as.
In the end, we believe that the key is to be able to prepare many "views that are divided into units that can be understood, but that also do not lose sight of the big picture.
[nishio.icon]
I think this is a very good question.
We'll need to think slowly to see if the AI's answers are good or not, or if we're missing something.
Q5. what is the access point for the general public to bring up "I want to do this"? Can I contact them directly?
Rather than suddenly DMing an individual, you should first
Related NPOs/Civic Organizations
Civic tech communities like Code for Japan
Municipal "Suggestion/Public Comment" window
It is realistic to go through a "place that is prepared as a receptacle" such as a "place that is prepared as a receptacle.

However, if you have a solid plan or question, contacting individuals directly is not necessarily a nuisance and is often more than welcome, as long as you "keep it short and to the point" and provide an easy way out to decline.
[nishio.icon]
AI is being kind, but in my opinion, the first thing to do is to say, "Do you want to? Then do it." I think.
If this response feels misguided, then you need to realize that the need expressed in the words "I want to do this" is "I want to do this, but I lack the thumbs up to do it, so you give it to me".
And since the person who was told this was suddenly being mugged, he or she said, "What? I'm not going to give it to you. and that's it.
Well, surprisingly, there are kind people who will let you out.
I think you should at least be aware that you are the one being mugged and not the one who has the right to get it fixed and served.
I think it's hard to get this across because when you really communicate directly with them, you don't say it so openly, you make it vague.
「 [It's been a week since I said I wanted to do it, and what did I get?] 」
Q6. what is the desired relationship between parliamentary democracy and digital direct democracy?
Not to replace one with the other,
Parliamentary system = representation and institutions with ultimate responsibility
Digital = Infrastructure to support agenda discovery, broad collection of opinions, and deliberation
I think it is realistic to have a division of labor called

The two-layered structure is digitally reinforced in the areas of broadly picking up "what should be on the agenda" and "what concerns are raised by which proposals," while leaving the final legalization and responsibility for the legislation to the Congress.
[nishio.icon]
Well, it feels that way.

I'm tempted to say, "Maybe we won't need legislators," and technically it will eventually be possible to build "a system that can do the same without them," but I think legislators will remain because there is no pathway for the decision to "eliminate them" in the moderate development path of a democratic state.
Q7. what if the divide is growing in Japan? Can non-face-to-face tools counter the agitation of social networking?
The division is
economic disparity
Fragmentation of the information environment (different media viewed)
A sense of helplessness that "my voice will not be heard."
accelerate when combined.
Whether non-face-to-face tools deepen or soften the divide depends on the design.
Designed to encourage one-sided spread and flames → Accelerated fragmentation
Dialogue tools designed so that "people from different positions know the most plausible arguments of the other side" → Reduces division
In this way, we believe it depends on the UI/UX and incentive design.
[nishio.icon]
I don't think it's "if we proceed," but "if we leave it alone, it will proceed."
We need to come up with as many "halting measures" as possible, and if they work, the division will stop.
If it doesn't work, there will be a civil war and the minority will die to end the division.
Q8. What is the role of politicians in an increasingly digital democracy?
From "the person who decides for me."
Facilitator to connect diverse opinions
Navigators who demonstrate a long-term vision
Design and protect transparent processes Rules Designer
I believe that the role of the company as a
I imagine that politicians will be required to have not only the skills to gather votes, but also "the ability to design and manage a forum for dialogue.
[nishio.icon]
Just as I wrote earlier, there is no "pathway through which the politicians will disappear", so the politicians themselves will remain.
As for individual politicians, each individual needs to discover some kind of civic appeal, and those who fail to discover it just fail to get elected and disappear.
There is no one way to appeal, and it's more advantageous to do what others can't.
Q9. wouldn't anonymous broad listening be effective for shy Japanese?
I think it is quite effective.
+1, There are a lot of people who want to be listened to but don't have the guts to talk.[nishio.icon]
Things you can't say "out of the air" if you use your real name.
Opinions that feel like a minority
By anonymously collecting "real opinions" and structuring them and returning them to politicians and administrators, the project will serve as a bridge between "real intentions" and "public nature.
However, because it is anonymous, it can also be rough, so it is important to design the operation to determine what questions to ask and how to handle discriminatory posts.
Q10. how do you trigger ethics and code updates within the company?
What is effective is to "make rules after the incident has occurred" before it happens,
1. turn around a kind of anonymous broad listening within the company,
Visualize the discomfort and gray areas felt in the field,
3. reflect the results in rules and guidelines
This is the cycle of

In Europe and the U.S., there are an increasing number of cases where employee surveys + workshops + policy revisions are conducted as a set. The point is not to create a policy once and never finish it, but to update it in small increments on the premise that it will be updated.
[nishio.icon]
I don't know why I asked this question.
I'm sure we'll see examples within the private sector first, because it's easier to do it within the private sector than it is in the public sector.
Q11. how do we not become alternatives to power and "think the power side is important too"?
Rather than creating an antagonistic "we are your enemies."
How broad listening and digital democracy contribute to existing policy goals (e.g., "reduce administrative costs," "strengthen accountability," etc.)
The shortcut is to be specific about the
In other words, we do not feel that an "alternative administration" is the way to go, but rather an approach that positions the existing power as a "supporting line" to do its job better.
[nishio.icon]
It's what you imagine by the word "power."
It seems that sometimes there are people who see it as an "anti-authority tool," but when I look at the Taiwan case, I don't think it's being used as an "anti-authority tool" at all.
Shouldn't we drop our assumptions and observe properly?
Even if you "listen to the opinions of many," if you don't have the power to act on them, you won't be able to achieve anything.

When the opposition used it to ask questions to the Prime Minister in the Japanese Diet, they had the "right to ask questions" independent of broad listening, not that the power they didn't have came to them through broad listening.
Q12: What can the IIDOBATA system do/what are the shortcomings/challenges?
What you can do:
Gather a wide range of opinions on a particular topic and group similar opinions together
Visualize minority opinions and share "there are other ways to feel this way".
Deficiencies/issues:
The "last step" of how to connect the gathered opinions to policies and concrete actions
How to compensate for the voices of those not participating (bias)
Resources and incentives for ongoing operations
Such as.
We have made progress in the opinion-gathering phase, but the challenge now is to connect that with the decision-making phase," he said.
[nishio.icon]
AI, you know exactly what you're talking about.
Q13. do digital technologies enhance "deliberation" or "populism"? What are the conditions?
It could be both.
Ranking and flame design to fuel only numbers → strengthen populism
Design that visualizes minority opinions and reasons, and emphasizes "why do you think so" → Supports deliberative discussion
Conditions,
1. that the algorithm evaluates not only "strong emotions" but also "well thought out reasons
2. the participation process is transparent and tampering is verifiable
is a big one.
[nishio.icon]
Don't think it's "technically easier to use it to enhance populism."
That's why the use of more populism became more prevalent first, and that's why we're in this situation.
We need to develop uses that curb populism, reduce division, and help people deliberate calmly
Well, I think if you make it, the entities that prefer populism will continue to use populist assistive technology.
Instead of "technology doing populism," "people using technology to do populism."
Q14. can broad listening be inclusive of those who are unable/alienated from being a party?
It's hard to "include everyone at once."
Anonymous: "I can say a few words anyway."
I see that others have the same alienation.
This is a much lower hurdle as an entry point.

However, it is difficult to reach people who do not know about the place or who do not have access to the Internet. Broad listening is not the only way to reach people, but it needs to be linked with offline venues, welfare, and education.
[nishio.icon]
Lowering the bar is, well, something we should do.
But, I don't think there's any need to call people who are not a party to the discussion to participate in the first place, so there's no need to try hard to call them together.
There are people who are involved but don't realize they're involved.
This isn't about broad listening, it's about sovereign education and all that.
Same story with people not participating in "voting," which is "a broad listening technique that has been realized over a long period of time for the entire population."
Q15. on the feeling that "Japan is 5-10 years behind
As you say, there is certainly a time lag between what happens in the world and what comes to Japan.
However, the amount of
You can also learn "what went wrong" with overseas cases in advance.
There is room for localization to adapt to the Japanese system and culture.
It can also be said that
I feel it is important to design with an awareness of "how to turn being a latecomer into an advantage," rather than "no because we are late.
[nishio.icon]
The image is that they are good at catching up after the black ships arrive and they feel a sense of crisis.
If the rest of the country collapses or if some of the Japanese municipalities collapse, they will get serious and do something about it.
Q16. what are the touchpoints of your digital democracy tools outside of politics?
Rather, there are many situations that are easier to introduce outside of politics. For example.
Decision-making within the company (feedback to benefits, work style, evaluation system)
Seeking input on curriculum improvement and campus environment at schools and universities
Policy making in community/condo management associations/NPOs
Such as.
We believe that by "gaining participation experience from familiar places in our daily lives," the hurdle for participation in political topics will gradually be lowered.
[nishio.icon]

Yes, it's "technology to support decision making by multiple people", so it has a wide variety of applications for people who know what they're doing, and it's easier to use it for decisions closer to home than to use it abstractly for "national politics" or something else that is distant from you.
Q17. can people use AI as a tool? What about safeguards?
Even if it is difficult to "master it completely."
Transparency Log
Third Party Audits
Multiple checks in high-risk areas (AI + human + another AI)
I believe that the decision-making process can be made better than that of human beings alone by combining
As a safeguard, it is not only a technical
regulation
Professional ethics (doctors, judges, government, etc.)
Citizen Surveillance
is required as a set.
[nishio.icon]
It's funny that you ask the question, "Can people use AI?"
With any technology, there will be people who can use it and people who can't.
For example, there are people who don't know how to use the tool called "fire", and there are hundreds of fires every year, but they don't say "let's stop using fire".
I think it's a good idea to build fire alarms and sprinklers as safeguards, so let's develop the technology.
Q18. i want to know what kind of tools are being created
A rough classification,
Broad listening systems: tools for collecting and clustering large numbers of citizens' voices
Deliberation support system: Tools for designing, recording, and visualizing small-group dialogues online
Policy participation system: pubic commentary and online voting and proposal platforms
Visualization system: Dashboards that show the distribution of opinions in maps and graphs
and others.
We feel that each is still in the development phase and will be integrated in the future.
[nishio.icon]
Well, something like that, it depends on your needs to integrate, I don't think it's right now.
Q19. "Visualization" of participants' thoughts and ideas and privacy
The point is to separate "raw data associated with individuals" from "aggregated and visualized results.
Raw data is strictly controlled and, as a rule, kept outside the company.
Statistical level information such as "There are about this many people in this position on this topic" is to be disclosed.
Visualize with a level of granularity that does not allow material to attack specific individuals.
The design should be such that
I think it is desirable for the community to reach a consensus on "how much to visualize" on a case-by-case basis.
[nishio.icon]
I think it's up to each person to decide what they feel is privacy, so I think it's best to be selective about what you want to disclose, and only what you want to disclose.
There will be no consensus in the community.
Q20. Why is digital democracy less likely to affect "major decisions" such as law reform?
The main reasons for the gap are
The process of changing the law itself is heavy and time consuming.
The existing side of the political process does not yet fully trust the new tools
There are no set "rules" for how to handle the results of digital participation.
Per.
In the short term, they tend to be treated as "reference materials",
I think it is possible to gradually increase the level of influence by clearly stating the rules, such as "always put on the agenda at the assembly" when certain conditions are met.
[nishio.icon]
Is it hard to do? On what basis did you make that judgment?
I know in the Taiwan case, digital democracy has led to a number of law reforms.
Isn't "hard to do" an assumption made by someone who hasn't seen the facts?
Q21. what is the "ultimate relationship" between representative government and digital democracy?
In my image,
Representative system: "decision-making layer" with responsibility and legal authority
Digital democracy: a "perceptual extension layer" that incorporates the "wisdom and senses of citizens" before and after its decisions
It is.

Ultimately, I think the goal is "a state where the process is so transparent and documented that the representatives cannot ignore the voice of the citizens. Rather than abolishing the representatives, the representatives will be redesigned as an interface with the citizens.
[nishio.icon]
I have no objection to an interpretation like that.
If this state of affairs were to be realized, whether the same amount of legislators would be needed as now is, well, debatable.
Q22. digital democracy = democracy in essence? Just a tool?
The essence is still a democratic issue of "who decides, how, and what," and we believe that AI and tools are the means to this end.
However, the design of the tool is
Which voice is easier to pick up?
Which voices are less visible?
In this sense, it can be said that "tool design" itself is becoming a new political issue, a "part of democracy," since it has a significant impact on
[nishio.icon]
Rather, "[collective decision-making]" was the first need, and "[voting]" was born as one of the ways to realize this need.
'The essence is "who decides who, how, and what"' is correct, but 'it is a matter of democracy' is not correct.
The method of [collective decision-making] does not have to be democratic.
Q23. where did you get the assumption that "digital democracy is superior even in a PLURAL society"?
I don't think it is a "proven truth" yet, but should be treated as a hypothesis that is worth testing because it may be so.
Rationale,
Potential to connect diverse populations that are difficult to connect offline alone
The ability to make visible minority voices that are often overlooked in majority rule
and others.

On the other hand, there are issues such as "how to handle people who cannot participate online" and "algorithm bias," and we believe that the only way forward is through experimentation and verification.
[nishio.icon]
>Where did you get the assumption that digital democracy is superior?
I feel like this is backwards.

I think digital democracy is "the activity of trying to create a better method of achieving democracy in a society in which digital technology exists than the method used to achieve democracy in earlier societies.
So digital democracy is necessarily "better than traditional democracy."
In a pluralistic society, it could be argued that national elections are unnecessary in the first place.
There is no evidence that it is a good idea to give equal voting rights to all members of a country, finding special meaning in the collective unit of the country.
The division of that "country" into MECE "prefectures" is even more unfounded.

Maybe the current form of the voting system was only created to lower administrative costs when the cost of administering the ballot was high, and when the cost of administering the ballot goes down, we'll have a form of more frequent voting in a more cluttered, intersecting set.
Q24. What kind of involvement do you have with companies?
Enterprises are
A "testing ground" for using digital democracy tools for decision-making within your company
Technology Partners" that work with local governments and NPOs to provide platforms and data analysis
Funding and resource providers" who support social experiments as sponsors.
It can be a
Rather than "meddling in politics," it is relatively easy to get involved in a positive way if you think about improving your company's governance and contributing to society as a set.
[nishio.icon]+1
Q25. What is your "device to attract interest" to raise awareness of the parties involved?
More than abstract politics,
Start with "specific themes directly related to your life.
Don't stop after one participation, but always provide feedback on "what happened afterwards".
Design it so that there is a bit of "discovery" or "learning" when you participate.
We feel it is important to

If you can reply, "Your opinion can be reflected in this way," or "I found this new point of view," rather than just saying, "Let me hear your opinion," your sense of ownership will gradually increase.
[nishio.icon]
>Start with "specific themes directly related to your life
This is a good way for that individual
It's expensive for the operator, because it's hard to know what themes are familiar to individual participants.
Before deciding on a theme, it might be a good idea to collect free descriptions and divide them into clusters with a broadband AI, etc.
I think it's okay to use the IIDOBATA system.
It's easier to do in a smaller municipality, because the degree to which municipal issues are familiar is higher.
Q26. Is it possible to prevent systematic "trolling" (mass introduction of biased voices) to BroadListen?
It cannot be completely prevented, but it can be significantly suppressed.
Technology to detect mass submissions from the same person or organization
Alerts of unnatural patterns (e.g., sudden spikes in only certain opinions)
Weighting down "bot-like clusters" in aggregate
and other technical measures.
In addition, transparency in the rules of the operation as to how it will handle any cases it finds will make it easier to maintain credibility.
[nishio.icon]
Personally, I think they should use my number to authenticate each individual and make it one per person.
Q27. What is the next "●ism" that will emerge as technology evolves?
The name has not yet been finalized, though,
A process-oriented approach in which the emphasis shifts from "who decides" to "what process and what information is used to decide.
Plurality-based principle where multiple actors coexist, including people and AI, states and citizens, companies and communities
We feel that the candidates are
In any case, I believe that we are not moving toward "one correct democracy," but rather toward a combination of several ways of doing things, depending on the situation.
[nishio.icon]
What will undoubtedly emerge will be the idea that "AI, which is better than humans, should govern."
Those who want to continue democracy ask, "Why don't people inferior to AI give up their sovereignty? Vested interests!" And they will be criticized.

Let [Claude Code] write [diary
[daily report]
An example can be found by [search in docs/diary https://scrapbox.io/nishio/search/page?search=docs%2Fdiary
code:CLAUDE.md
### LOG.md
- A place to write **work logs** in that repository.
- This is to recall how far the work has been done in the event that a running agent is suddenly terminated by some accident.
- Keep a **chronological and detailed** record of commands executed, things tried, results, etc.
- AI will **always record any code or setting changes in LOG.md. **
### PLAN.md
- **A single file for "plans in progress". **
- Organize "where are we going now with this project" rather than a to-do list.
- After planning, follow the rules for each repository.
- Move it to `docs/diary/completed_plans/` or something similar,
- Leave a summary in the DIARY and then archive it.
### docs/diary/*.md
- A place to write a **comprehensive recap** of the day's or session's **work.
- Example: `docs/diary/2025-11-25.md`.
- Assuming LOG.md is "real-time" and "sequential logging",
- A diary is **a summary/reflection written at the end of the day**.
- Even when the AI writes automatically, it should be a sentence that **makes sense when read by a human being**.
### CLAUDE.md
- A place to write **"knowledge to remember every time "** specific to that repository.
### docs/*.md
- A place to write repository-specific "knowledge that you may need to refer to repeatedly, but not so much that you need to remember it every time.
- It is useless if you forget what you wrote, so write in CLAUDE.md what you wrote and where.

pages.title: Motivation caused by lack of information

lines.text: Motivation caused by lack of information

In a time when people did not share the feeling of those who had what they did not have, they felt that having something that they did not have would make them very happy, and this caused a strong motivation to have it.
With the development of [information sharing], this "[motivation] caused by [lack of information]" will decrease.
[the grass is always greener on the other side]
For example, marriage

In an era when all the older women around them were married, older women would say things like, "Marriage is a woman's happiness," and unmarried women who heard this would have a fear that they would be very unhappy if they didn't get married, and I think this gave them a very strong motivation to get married.

The development of social networking has shared that unmarried arabs are not very unhappy and that married people are not full of happiness, and marriage or not has turned into a choice where you can choose both.
For example, rich people
In the days when things like Hikakin's videos of him buying foreign cars and such were only aired on TV in those areas, there was a strong admiration for rich celebrities and a desire to be one too.

However, if information is also shared about Hikakin's daily work style that would be "extremely black labor if he were a company employee," more people will have the feeling that they don't want to work that hard and want to live a leisurely life.
When you can observe people on social media who have money but seem unhappy, etc., the appeal of having money diminishes.
In the first place, there is a diminishing utility, so getting too much will not make you happy.
I think this change is irreversible.
Like [the law of increasing entropy].

Deep Researcher with Test-Time Diffusion
[2507.16075 Deep Researcher with Test-Time Diffusion https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16075]
>[Yamori_ds https://x.com/Yamori_ds/status/1996477837390275039] [Deep research], which was a must-read paper on creating smart report-based AI agents.
> They say that by creating an initial draft full of noise, working in parallel with multiple Agents, and repeating self-improvement, you can efficiently produce a quality report.
> It's called Diffusion, but it's tricky to be LLM.
Yasuno told me.
[GPT5.icon] https://chatgpt.com/c/6933e66a-47f0-8320-b870-1abc870af634
In a nutshell,

This is a paper that says, "We enhanced Deep Research agents with a "diffusion model-like" test-time algorithm and outperformed existing DRs such as OpenAI Deep Research. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
What is the paper you want to solve?
Deep Research agents (OpenAI Deep Research, Perplexity, Grok, HuggingFace Open-DR, GPT Researcher, etc.) that are currently in vogue are
With a mishmash of "scaling at test" like CoT, best-of-n, self-refine, debate, MCTS,
Not designed to look at the entire report you write.
When writing long reports, information gets lost in the middle or the structure breaks down.
He raises the issue that there is a limitation that ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
The authors therefore propose a Deep Research agent that explicitly models the generation of long research reports as a "diffusion process.
Proposal: Test-Time Diffusion Deep Researcher (TTD-DR)
The idea is simple: treat the human research and writing process = like a sampling of diffusion models. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
0. first define the "backbone" DR agent
The base DR agent (Backbone DR Agent) consists of 3 stages: ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
1. Stage 1: Research Plan Generation
Create a "report structure, chapters, and list of research topics" from the user's query.
Here is the scaffold for all subsequent searches and summaries.
Stage 2: Iterative Search and Synthesis (RAG-like loop)
2a: Generate the question "What should I search next?
2b: Search the Web and create a "summary" of relevant documents
Repeat the loop 2a-2b until the plan is well covered.
3. Stage 3: Final Report Generation
The Stage 1 plan and the QA columns from Stage 2 were combined to generate the final report.
Up to this point, we have been "a rather normal and proper DR agent".
1. "Draft→sequential revision" as a diffusion process
The "Test-Time Diffusion" idea is plugged in here: ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
1. one shot generation of initial draft (noisy report) by LLM alone
Have them write a long report anyway, using only user queries + internal knowledge.
This is considered a "noisy, incomplete/inaccurate draft".
2. look at the draft and decide "what to look into next".
Enter the current draft into Stage 2a (Search Question Generation),
Generate search queries by looking at where there are holes, dubious claims, or missing perspectives.
3. "Denoise" the draft in the search results
Using information retrieved and summarized by Stage 2b,
Add or revise the draft to reduce "noise" (ambiguities, omissions, and errors).
(4) Rotate this "search->revise" loop for several steps.
Each step makes the draft a little better = analogy of the denoising step in the diffusion model.
After the loop is completed, the final report is rewritten and completed using the entire accumulated history.
The point is that the draft itself is used as a "state that guides the next search".
By this,
Rather than searching in sections separately and then merging them,
It claims that information can be added while maintaining consistency and context throughout the report. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Component-wise Self-Evolution of each agent
Another pillar is Self-Evolution.([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Plan generation, Search Question generation, Answer summary, final Report generation, etc,
Each "unit agent" is
Sampling multiple candidates
Screening by some score (e.g., diversity, coverage, or LLM-as-a-judge)
Replaced with a better configuration
The algorithm is self-improving only during testing in the form of
By this,
Increased diversity and depth of search queries,
The "complexity / amount of information" of the information obtained is increased,
The analysis shows that report quality increases as a result. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Experiments and Results
benchmark
Evaluated on the following "long research" and "multi-step reasoning" tasks: ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
LongForm Research (long research report generation)
DeepConsult (more specialized consultative tasks)
HLE-Search / HLE-Full (Highly Difficult Search + Inference QA)
GAIA (complex multi-step QA)
Evaluation Method:
Side-by-side comparison based on Helpfulness / Comprehensiveness
A proportionally solid evaluation design that calibrates LLM-as-a-judge with human annotation and then uses it for automatic evaluation. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Main figures
Side-by-side comparison with OpenAI Deep Research.
69.1% / 74.5% win rate (% of TTD-DR judged better) for 2 long tasks. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Also in HLE systems and GAIA,
Much more accurate than a simple LLM + search,
It also outperforms OpenAI Deep Research in many metrics (only GAIA narrowly loses -> reversed in final TTD-DR). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Comparing the same computation time (latency),
Backbone → +Self-Evolution → +Diffusion with Retrieval
The analysis also shows that the "performance improvement per latency" is greater the more you add to the "performance improvement per latency". ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
In short, the selling point is that it can produce better output than existing Deep Research products at about the same inference cost.
What are the new/interesting points?
I'll just focus on what seems important to me personally:
1. "Draft-centric" DR agent design
While most DR agents have a "plan → search by section → merge at the end" structure,
This is designed so that you always have a "whole draft" with you at all times to search and revise. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
2. bringing the metaphor of the diffusion model into the test-time algorithm
Consider the generation process as "draft with noise → de-noise step iteration",
The loop that combines draft and search in both directions is neatly formulated as an algorithm. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Use Self-Evolution on a "per-agent" basis
Plan / Question / Answer / Report by evolving each during testing,
They are trying to reduce the information degradation that occurs in long agent chains. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])
Organization of evaluation protocols for Deep Research agents
Helpfulness / Comprehensiveness + LLM-as-a-judge Organized an evaluation framework called calibration.
Potential baseline for evaluation for the DR agent research community.
Brief summary
Deep Research Agent Design,
"The Human Research & Writing Process ≈ Denoising the Diffusion Model."
The response was reorganized with the following response,
Test-Time Diffusion," which revolves around drafts, searches, and revisions.
TTD-DR is a combination of "Self-Evolution of each component."
The paper shows that it outperformed existing DR, including OpenAI Deep Research, on many benchmarks. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2507.16075v1])

If you want an explanation from the perspective of "I want to incorporate it into my DR workflow / create a similar structure" (pseudo code level, how to mimic evaluation design, etc.), I can break it down and explain from that perspective.
There are. There are two systems that can be roughly divided into "TTD-DR almost itself" and "conventional Deep Research OSS".
1. OSS that implements TTD-DR quite faithfully

OptILLM's `deep_research` tool

One of the tools, `deep_research`, clearly states "Test-Time Diffusion Deep Researcher (TTD-DR) is implemented.
It is a Python library with a Selenium-based web_search + TTD-DR loop, so it is easy to handle for calling from your own code.
1-4. TTD-RAG (application implementation for competition)
Repository: `eamag/MMU-RAG-competition` ([GitHub https://github.com/eamag/MMU-RAG-competition?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
The agent is called `TTD-RAG`, created for the MMU-RAG Competition, and the README states that it "faithfully implements the framework of the TTD-DR paper.

*The Google mainframe guides the product version on Agentspace, but does not release the code as OSS. ([Google Research https://research.google/blog/deep-researcher-with-test-time-diffusion/])
2. related "Deep Research" OSS (before/around TTD-DR)
OSSs that are/were close to the TTD-DR baseline of thought:
2-1. LangChain system
`langchain-ai/local-deep-researcher`

Local LLM (Ollama/LM Studio) + web search agent that runs several rounds of "search, summarize, detect gaps, search again" to produce a final Markdown report. ([GitHub https://github.com/langchain-ai/local-deep-researcher?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Famous Deep Research agent. A "Deep Research" mode has recently been added. ([GitHub https://github.com/assafelovic/gpt-researcher?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
`nickscamara/open-deep-research` etc.

lines.text: Cultural Preferences for Formal versus Intuitive Reasoning
[PDF https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1207/s15516709cog2605_4]
[GPT5.icon]
What this study showed (super summary)
1. people have "two reasoning systems"
FORMAL: Follow rules, logic, and definitions
INTUITIVE: follow intuition, analogy, context, and belief
2. European-Americans are more likely to switch to "rules first".
When rules and intuition collide,
Easy to classify and determine as per rules
relatively unaffected by typicality or "believability" (at least at first).
3. East Asians (Chinese and Koreans) tend to put "intuition first
Even if there are rules,
Similar examples (exemplar)
Category Typicality
The "believability" of the conclusion
Tend to be strongly drawn to
Logically OK, but if it's "intuitively strange," it's likely to be perceived as less convincing.
Asian-Americans are "middle" or "leaning American."
East Asian culture at home, American culture in school and society
→ Reasoning style is often an in-between pattern as well.
5. cultural differences in "which tools are prioritized for use" rather than differences in ability
If you have them do only abstract logic tasks, there is almost no cultural difference.
There are virtually no cultural differences in assignments solved by intuition alone.
When the two sides collide, which takes precedence is different.
6. neither is "right".
Formal Preference: Strong in logic test and rule tasks, but also prone to context-ignoring errors
intuitive preference: strong in context, relationships, and experience, but prone to more "belief-losing" errors in logic tests
→ Ideally, it should be possible to use both depending on the situation.
In a nutshell:
The same brain hardware can be used in different cultures.
The "voice of logic" or the "voice of intuition" has a different priority.
...and this study shows quite nicely in four experiments.

Super Modular Production
Super modular production, not surprisingly, was not mentioned.
[GPT5.icon]
To put it bluntly,
When the inputs used for production are "complementary," that [production function] is [supermodular].
This is the story.
1. intuitive meaning
Consider a function (f(x,y)) that is produced using two inputs (x, y) (e.g., "skilled labor" and "advanced machinery").
The marginal productivity (how much extra output is increased) when (x) is increased is
(y) the more you use it, the bigger it gets.
→ "(x) and (y) are complementary (compatible)"
This property of "marginal productivity enhancing each other" is called supermodular. ([IDEAS/RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/p/oxf/wpaper/795.html])
So what is super modular production,
A production structure in which inputs are complementary to each other, and the more one is increased, the more effective the other becomes.
It is only necessary to understand that it is about the same.
2. a little more formal (in the case of production functions)
Suppose the production function (f(x_1,\dots,x_n)) is smooth enough. In this case
\frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i \partial x_j} \ge 0 \quad (i \neq j)
is true for all combinations,
(f) is called a supermodular production function. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supermodular_function])
This means "the more input factors (x_j) are used, the greater the incremental effect of a small increase in (x_i)" = incremental differences.
3. what makes you happy economically
With super modular production functions, you get all sorts of beautiful properties:
1. complementarity of elemental demand
If the production function is super modular, when the price of a factor falls
It can be shown that the demand for that element as well as "the demand for other elements increases together".
(Factors of production are complementary goods to each other). ([IDEAS/RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/p/oxf/wpaper/795.html])
2. positive-assertive matching
In a matching model (e.g., high-skilled workers and high-performance machinery, marriage between highly educated people, etc.),
If the production (or utility) function is supermodular.
Positive correlation matching is optimal,
(Becker type result). ([Leland D. Crane https://ldcrane.github.io/files/spm-and-search-2018.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. comparative statics (comparative statics) become monotonous
When moving parameters such as price and technology, it is easier to guarantee that the optimal solution will "move monotonically"
(Theories of comparative statics such as Topkis, Milgrom & Roberts). ([IDEAS/RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/p/oxf/wpaper/795.html])
4. a very simple image example
Example: IT investment (servers and software) and skilled engineers
Increasing IT investment alone will not be fully utilized if there are no talented engineers.
On the other hand, even if there are only excellent engineers, the old system is not powerful enough.
When both are increased together, productivity growth "adds up to more than
This kind of "more efficient to increase collectively" structure,
This is an image of super modular production.
If you also want to know "how it relates to matching theory (Becker)" or "how it differs from sub-modular production," I will delve into that as well.

pages.title: I can do it, but it's exhausting.

lines.text: I can do it, but it's exhausting.

>If you look at people with developmental disabilities only in terms of whether or not they can do something, you are misjudging them. Between 'can' and 'can't,' there are a lot of things that are 'doable but exhausting.'

[What is necessary to support developmental disabilities? Is "Praise when it's done" a cautionary tale? Interview with Dr. Toru Yoshikawa, child psychiatrist -- CM producer depicting developmental disabilities [Serial #Living with Invisible Disabilities] [LITALICO Developmental Navigator] https://h-navi.jp/column/article/ 35028186]

>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1564931206910984192] I always tell teachers at trainings that developmental disabilities lie somewhere between "I can do it without problems" and "I can't do it despite my best efforts" - "I can do it but it's exhausting. I always tell teachers in trainings that developmental disabilities lie between "doable without problems" and "not doable despite their best efforts". If we continue to impose this "doable but tiring" on the individual, he/she will eventually become exhausted and unstable, or develop a secondary disability.

>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1564931208399945728] What we need to pay special attention to is the type of child who does not act out much and whose stress is directed toward our home, and the teachers tend to overlook his/her sense of trouble because he/she is not in trouble on the surface. This type of child tends to be overlooked by teachers because he or she is not in trouble on the surface. I feel that this type of child is more common in girls with ASD who do not have intellectual problems.

>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1564931209603747842] So it is rather a bad idea to say that you don't have to give consideration to them because they are doing their best, or rather that making them do their best will lead to independence. It is important to make the classroom a "comfortable space" and the class a "comfortable time to concentrate on learning" by giving positive consideration.
>[umikotam https://x.com/umikotam/status/1565003119582334976] Excuse me. Let me ask you a question.
> Most of the activities in my life are full of "I can do it, but I'm tired" > "I'll do my best," and I'm exhausted every day,
> I thought everyone was forcing themselves to live doing "doable but exhausting" things. That's why I was trying so hard too.
> Is that actually not the case?

>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1565090511429726211] Since "tiredness" is a feeling that only the individual can understand, there is no objective way to show how tired other people get when they work hard. I know, right? Therefore, we think "people around me must be working this hard too".
> I think it is important to think, "Perhaps I am trying too hard.
>[snooze_kakkun https://x.com/snooze_kakkun/status/1565108216832598016] I apologize for my lack of knowledge.
> I know this is a very sensitive subject,
> What is the boundary between developmental disabilities and laziness,
> Does that mean that the judgment itself varies a lot?
> I can do my best to have fun myself, though,
> I feel like I get sick (tired) of things I don't like very quickly.

>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1565113857944993792] Basically, I think it's best to avoid making comparisons between developmentally disabled or lazy. I think the label "lazy" implies "not trying hard enough," but in the first place, effort is not something that others can look at from the outside and judge whether it is enough.
>[ChanPchanSniper https://x.com/ChanPchanSniper/status/1565172200386113537] I can do it, but it's exhausting, and I've been doing it lately.
> Muscle training for half therapeutic purposes, preparation regarding your own work, minimal daily living, hobbies, search for developmental and mental illness devises...
> What happens to the human body if you keep doing that?　I'm tired every day and it's very hard to get up early in the morning. .... Please let me know what to do!
>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1565175141566656512] It's difficult.

> I often advise that when you are feeling well, you should set a standard that says "I am at my limit when this happens" and decide in advance that you will take a break or distance yourself when those signs appear. If it is difficult for you to recognize the signs by yourself, it may be a good idea to consult with your doctor or a counselor.

>[Yk5cVb https://x.com/Yk5cVb/status/1565347274984947717] I know there are different types of developmental disabilities, but is being extremely clumsy a trait? I have always found it hard to live with.

> Even if you practice hundreds of times, such as hand games or simple dance repetitions like Alps 10,000 Shaku, you may be able to do it by chance, but you will not be able to do it. You will fail at the next attempt.
> Half a century of avoiding and escaping

>[tep_kikuchi https://x.com/tep_kikuchi/status/1565466081552384001] It is up to the physician to determine if the disorder actually meets the proper diagnostic criteria, but there is a developmental coordination disorder (DCD), a disorder whose main symptom is clumsiness. There is a developmental disorder called Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD), whose main symptom is clumsiness. I thought this might be helpful.

[organization] consists of [connection of persons
An organization is not just [a group of people], but [resources accumulated in the organization
This resource allows us to produce more efficiently than people outside the organization.
This is why organizations can generate the energy to stay in shape.
Organizations that cannot "produce more efficiently than those outside" lose "the energy to stay in shape" and fall apart.
For example, more productive organizations offer products at lower prices to steal customers or offer better treatment to attract employees.
One of these resources is the "people connection."
[Destroying the Prisoner's Dilemma by placing an observer]
[Improved communication efficiency through a common language].
[The emulator of organizational culture.]
Situation 1
Mr. A and Mr. B are communicating.
No one else.
Mr. B might react quickly or slowly to Mr. A's movement in this situation.
This is the nature of Mr. B
Situation 2
Mr. A and Mr. B are communicating.
but unlike situation 1, Mr. B is connected to other C, D, and E.
If Mr. B is a member of a corporate organization, there's often this connection.
If Mr. A does not observe it, it appears to be no different from situation 1 from Mr. A's point of view
But even if Mr. B's nature doesn't change, changes in social structure will add overhead.
Response time overhead
Assume that a response is made in one credit hour that Mr. B can determine independently.
If C, D, and E require confirmation, even under the best conditions (others respond in 1 unit time and can be executed in parallel), it takes +1 unit time.
In general, some people are slow to respond and there are dependencies in communication.
Communcation cost overhead
Suppose A communicates at a cost of one unit.
When B can respond alone, the cost is 1 unit, but if confirmation is needed from C, D, or E, B pays +3 units of communication cost.
This is the principle of "I can't handle it if you keep coming at me so hard.

pages.title: Difficulties with Performing if not connected to social field.

lines.text: Difficulties with Performing if not connected to social field.
>The connection with [Social Field] in [Presensing] is not happening, so we have difficulties in the [Performing] stage.
from  [Nodal Point of Thought 2025-05-03]
[GPT5.icon]
In the context of U-theory, that sentence roughly says this kind of causation:
First, the meaning of the term

[Presencing]: presence + sensing. "The explanation is that you will be in a state where you can move from the possibility of [the future that is rising], rather than from the possibility of [an extension of the present] (past habits). ([MIT Sloan https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents?PublicationDocumentID=10093])

[Social field": The "atmosphere," "quality of relationships," and "pattern of interaction" that lies before the content of individual comments (that thing you feel in your body when you enter the room, such as "I feel nervous"). It is difficult to grasp just by observing from the outside, but it is possible to understand by entering and "becoming it". ([Medium https://medium.com/presencing-institute-blog/social-fields-shifting-the-quality-of-our-collective-being-6bfc8de3afac])

[Performing]: The stage of "making/expanding" what has been created to function in a "[scene (of a play, movie, etc.)] ([system]). As a metaphor, it is necessary to "play" the "big (macro) violin (the whole surrounding = the scene)" rather than the "small violin (the action at hand)," and it is necessary to convene the appropriate players and to [jointly] create the "scene" in order for multiple actors to move from "discussion" to "[joint creation]". creation]" from "debate" to "[joint creation]". ([MIT Sloan https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents?PublicationDocumentID=10093])
What's in "No Connection, Performing Stuck"
No "connection" to the social field in presencing =

[The state of making a proposal only with the head without grasping the "reality of the place" such as [unspoken rules of the place], [trust] wiring, who has what [pain]/[pride]/[fear], where [mines] are, what is [legitimacy]...etc. The state in which a proposal is made only with the mind without grasping the "reality of the place" such as [[somesthesis]] including [[mine]], what [legitimacy] is....
If you go straight to the right side (Prototyping→Performing), you will not be able to do what you need to do in Performing:
"[Who should be involved]" is off (no correct [key person] / call on them in the wrong order).

"The field does not switch from [discussion to co-creation]" ([resistance], [cynicism], and [dividing into parts] are preserved) ([MIT Sloan https://mitsloan.mit.edu/ shared/ods/documents?PublicationDocumentID=10093])

As a result, even if the prototype itself works, [friction costs] explode during the adoption, continuation, and scale phases (paying for the "[referral responsibility system], [loss of trust], and [boardroom]" in your note).

In other words, Performing is not only a matter of "implementation skills," but also a matter of "can you play the place as an instrument?" If you do not have the necessary "how to play the instrument of the place" in presencing, you will stumble in the end. ([MIT Sloan https://mitsloan.mit.edu/shared/ods/documents?PublicationDocumentID=10093])
I'll take your note as an example.

When A enters a new community, if it moves only with "[this is the way it should be]" without connecting to the [social field] (the existing [trust network]), it may be "[the right theory]" in the short term, but Performing (= [make it work within the relationship ]], [turning collaboration around], [increasing referrals]) is likely to fail.
The bankruptcy cost is passed on to [referrer] B and [existing member], not A - this is where your "[cosigner]" metaphor corresponds.
Practical check (is it connected?)
When the connection is made presencingly, at least the following can be verbalized:
What is "[what is protected]/[what is feared]" in this place?
What increases or decreases trust in the situation (what is considered "taking money out of the wallet")?
What is the relationship diagram of major players and what are the procedures ([meeting body], [ritual], [manner of agreement]) to move to co-creation?
If you proceed with ambiguity here, you will usually catch fire in Performing.

pages.title: Influences formed outside of our field of vision

lines.text: Influences formed outside of our field of vision

>[weiwei882288 https://x.com/weiwei882288/status/2003474806793240814] Historically in Japanese society, while making a sharp distinction between "inside (seima)" and "outside (world)," in effect "[seima]" was almost all the world needed for survival. The geographical conditions of an island nation, a single language, and a single culture made it difficult to survive. Under the geographical conditions of an island nation, a monolingual society, and a social structure based on village communities, there was little need to constantly negotiate with other civilizations, and [the world's opinion] = [the world] was everything. Thus, "[seima]" functioned well enough as a substitute for the original world, and the Japanese did not need to develop a metacognition to perceive the world in a relative manner.

> Since the Meiji era, Japan joined the international community as a modern nation, introducing diplomacy based on international law and a global capitalist economy. However, although the institutions and formalities were modernized, the assumptions of people's cognition were not updated, and the sense that "the world = the world" remained preserved. As a result, it became easier to apply Japan's internal common sense and logic directly to the outside world, treating foreigners and other cultures not as "subjects of the world" but as "objects that can be evaluated and processed according to internal standards. The very idea of ascertaining what kind of [log], [network], and [influence] an outsider has is weak.

> Furthermore, in Japanese society, influence is easily understood as something visible and within the system, such as titles, organizations, and seniority. On the other hand, influence in the contemporary world is often quietly formed outside of Japanese people's [view], such as in [informal] [diaspora networks] and [professional communities], from online to offline, across borders and languages. Because it is impossible to imagine these "[invisible] influences" only from within the Japanese "[world]," we tend to disregard and exclude foreigners who are not adapted to the context of Japanese society, as well as others who appear to be unknown. As a result, they unknowingly make enemies of those who have influence in another coordinate system, and this structure will later rebound back to their reality in a detrimental way.
I think I understood something close to this through a different route.
Just as there is the world as the inner world and the world as the outer world, there is the internal world and the external world.

At a time when I didn't know how to build my reputation in the internal world, being recognized outside the company made me think, "I don't have to worry too much about my reputation in the internal world.
Originally, the PhD was an evaluation axis that didn't fit within the confines of a particular company.
Experts tend to have professional communities outside the company
Operate in areas outside the company that are not yet very visible from within the company, gain influence, and then come back with something of value to the company.
In 2025, Audrey Tang came to Cybozu's Nihonbashi office and shot a video interview with the president as a clear example.
In 2012 [the birth of Cybozu-style], the culture was transmitted outside the company, and outside the company was recognized for its transmission.
This had the effect of strengthening their influence within the company after the fact.

>[weiwei882288 https://x.com/weiwei882288/status/2003474806793240814] While the Western "culture of guilt" presupposes an internalized conscience, the Japanese "culture of shame" -- Ruth Benedict's classic analysis -- takes the public gaze as the absolute arbiter.

> In this structure, morality and justice become synonymous with public approval. The principle of action is not "whether it is right" but "how the world sees it. This leads to strong social integration, but at the same time it makes imagination about the outside of the world unnecessary. Since the world is everything, evaluations outside the world are irrelevant.

> Herein lies the origin of the epistemological fallacy that "the world = the world. Japanese people are extremely sensitive to the evaluation of the "world," but structurally insensitive to the evaluation of the "world" outside the "world" (non-Japanese language speech space, diaspora networks crossing national borders, specialized communities unrelated to ethnic units, etc.). ) is structurally insensitive to the "world" outside of the "between. This is because historically it has not been associated with "worldliness" as it relates to survival and recognition.
[GPT5.icon]
The claim of the presenting post is largely,

Historically in Japan, "inside = the world" was almost all that existed in the world of life, and since worldly affairs/exclusion determined life and death, there was little need to relativize the "outside = the world".

After the Meiji era, only the system was modernized and the assumption of recognition (the world = global sense) remained, so external influences (cross-border networks, etc.) were overlooked and landmines were stepped on.
This can be explained by the "culture of shame/culture of sin" (Benedict).
...I think that is the line of reasoning. If you look at it critically, the weaknesses are rather clear.
The historical narrative is "too strong."

The "island nation, single language, village community → poor constant negotiations with different civilizations" is easy to understand in one aspect, but it is a rough generalization. Even in the Edo period, external trade (Nagasaki) and diplomacy (e.g., Korean envoys) continued, and "the country as a whole was not connected to the outside world" is easily an overstatement. ([Nippon https://www.nippon.com/en/features/c00104/foreign-relations-in-early-modern-japan-exploding-the-myth-of-national-seclusion .html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(Rather, the point of contention would be "who had contact with the outside world = bias in hierarchy/region.")
There is an image of "Japan = the same old Japanese only for everyone," but in reality, it was much messier than that.
Big difference in dialects

In the past, regional differences were stronger than now, and there were situations where mutual understanding was difficult even with the same "Japanese" (i.e., internal "translation" was necessary).
There are minority languages
For example, there are different languages within Japan, such as Ryukyuan and Ainu (i.e., there are "different cultures" within Japan).
Some foreign words.
Certain segments of the population were involved with foreign languages, such as Chinese and Dutch (i.e., not zero negotiations with the outside world).
The assumption that "the world" is monolithic is dangerous.

However, in reality, there can be different "worlds" for different statuses, regions, genders, etc., and the world itself changes with modernization, migration, and industrial structure. In fact, there is a cautious argument that "each world" can exist according to status, region, gender, etc., and that the nature of the world itself changes with modernization, migration, and industrial structure. ([hokuriku-u.ac.jp https://www.hokuriku-u.ac.jp/library/libraryDATA/kiyo55/econ01.pdf])
From this perspective, it is more likely to be a question of which of several worlds is being referred to, rather than the "world = world fallacy.
The "culture of shame/culture of sin" is useful, but academically it's a knife.

The Benedictine framework itself can easily become a "blunt instrument of dichotomy" and is often criticized; Lummis critically discusses the strong influence of "[The Chrysanthemum and the Sword]" as a political document (rather than an accurate statement) and the mass production of dichotomous tools. ([Asia-Pacific Journal: Japan Focus https://apjjf.org/c-douglas-lummis/2474/article])

There are also early criticisms (references to Dore and others) of the "shame-type/guilt-type" division of comparative culture itself. ([J-STAGE https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jsr1950/27/4/27_4_63/_article])
Therefore, it is easy to slip into "Nihonjinron-ish essentialism" when this framework is used as the main engine.
Meaning of "slippery slope to Japenological essentialism."
Essentialism:
To treat the Japanese as if they have a fixed essence (Japanese are this kind of race/ethnicity).
Nihonjinron-like:
A type of argument that broadly states "Japan is special" or "Japanese people are like this."
The biggest one is the "leap of causality.
"Poor negotiation with the outside world" → "Metacognition is not developed."
"shame-centered" → "can't imagine outside influences"

This leap cannot be asserted without psychological and sociological data. As an explanation, it is fascinating, but the weak verifiability (ambiguous disproving conditions) makes it difficult for the argument to be more than a "sticking story".
Some alternative explanations are more straightforward.
"Missing the world's appreciation" is more than the essence of culture, for example.
Language barriers and bias in information distribution
Degree to which careers and resource allocation are closed in the domestic system (academia, government, and business)
Incentives to rationalize optimization for domestic use
Many things can be explained by If you don't hold this point, the story will be moralized like a "flaw of the Japanese people".
Summary: How to rephrase it to make it stronger
This assertion is sharp as a general statement: "If you optimize for a closed evaluation system (the world), you will have accidents in another evaluation system (the world).

However, if we do not focus on ethnic characteristics such as "Japanese people are not able to do this," but rather include (1) the multilayered nature of the world, (2) differences in time, class, and region, and (3) incentives and the information environment, the resistance to criticism will increase dramatically.

lines.text: The birth of the Cybozu Method
[GPT5.icon]
Time of appearance (since when?)
Cybozu opened [Cybozu style] as Cybozu's own media in May 2012. ([cybozu.co.jp https://cybozu.co.jp/company/history/])

On May 14, 2012, shortly after the launch, the first editor-in-chief, [Yukio Ohtsuki], clearly stated the aims and policies in an article titled "Why Cybozu is starting its own media". ([Cybozu-style https://cybozushiki.cybozu.co.jp/?p=139])
Initial aims (based on description at the time)

The concept is a collaboration and IT information site for "[teams that create new value]". The site talks about the lack of information on "team x business x collaboration" while there is a lot of information on tools for individuals and "office (box)-centered" information. ([cybozu.co.jp https://cybozu.co.jp/company/history/])

The editorial policy is based on "what I want to know," and the editorial department declares that it will create articles that it itself wants to read (i.e., it will not lean toward "advertising that the company wants to say"). ([Cybozu style https://cybozushiki.cybozu.co.jp/?p=139])

The company's explanation is that while it started in May 2012 with the aim of enhancing the company's brand value, it does not publish articles for product promotion or recruitment purposes, and does not place any emphasis on PV supremacy. ([Business Insider Japan https://www.businessinsider.jp/article/177899/])

As background context, there is a look back that sales were flat at the time and there was an atmosphere of "let's try something new," and they tried again at the timing of the popularization of SNS. ([PR Magazine https://blog.cd-j.net/seminar-report/cybozu/])

The company also explained that it focused on communicating the value of "how the way of working will change" and the attitude of the company and its employees rather than the product itself, with the starting points of "creating a new customer base" and "approaching potential customers in the younger demographic. ([Six Apart K.K. - CMS software and blogging service provider https://www.sixapart.jp/business/cybozu.html])
Supplemental structure (initial members)

The first editor-in-chief was Yukio Otsuki, who was replaced by [Yoshimitsu Fujimura] as the second editor-in-chief in January 2015. ([Cybozu-style https://cybozushiki.cybozu.co.jp/articles/m000405.html])

Social Jenga

>[sitasimiyasui https://x.com/sitasimiyasui/status/2002377312864776412] [Jenga (Brazilian brand of haloperidol)] is a game of finding "parts that do not collapse when pulled out. I tried to pull out "[Christ]" from [Christianity], and it turned out to be OK, so [capitalism] was born as a result.
>[Maguro_Kana https://x.com/Maguro_Kana/status/2002591532562722935] If you remove the [authority] that guarantees it from the [power structure], the structure is maintained.
> because all but the lunatics act as if authority exists: ......
> It's interesting that you use this as a metaphor for Jenga.
>[Maguro_Kana https://x.com/Maguro_Kana/status/2002591765870907490] No, well, is the structure really holding? It's slowly crumbling and you just haven't noticed it? If you ask me, I don't know.
[GPT5.icon]
This series of statements is roughly a "Jenga" metaphor for the following three things.
1) There are "components that do not collapse when pulled out" (i.e., core-like components do not actually carry the load).
In Jenga, there are "components that collapse when pulled out" and "components that hold up surprisingly well even when pulled out. The same is true of social systems and ideologies,
While principles, myths, and authority (justification) "seem to be at the center".
In fact, institutions, customs, interests, technology, and infrastructure support the load.
Even if the "center-like object" is removed, the shape is retained for a while.
The intuition that.
2) What do you mean by "it was okay to remove Christ from Christianity -> capitalism"?
This is a provocative compression rather than a strictly historical proposition here. What I want to say is probably:
Even though modernization and secularization have weakened Christ as a faith

The "lifestyle" and systems of discipline, diligence, contract, guilt/conscience, time management, letter culture, and organizational management that had been created by Christian societies until then remained.
On top of that, markets, profit, and investment were added, and as a result, capitalism turned.
In short, "even if the "meaning" of religion fades, the "pattern" (system and mode of behavior) created by religion can remain.
(However, it is messy to explain the causes of the establishment of capitalism solely in terms of Christian deformation, and there are tons of counter-arguments.)
[nishio.icon]Discussed in connection with "The Ethics of Protestantism and the Spirit of Capitalism."
[GPT5.icon]It pretty much meshes with the core of Weber's "The Ethics of Protestantism and the Spirit of Capitalism" (and the bitter conclusion at the end of the book).
1) "Capitalism remains even if Christ is removed" = "the type of action" remains autonomous even if the "religious motivation" disappears.
Weber's plot goes roughly like this.
The Calvinist theory of the schedule creates anxiety that "I don't know if I'm on the side of salvation."
That anxiety is "channeled" into an ethic (intra-secular asceticism) that keeps us ascetically committed to our vocation (calling / Beruf).

As a result, capital accumulation accelerates as profits are reinvested through diligence and temperance while avoiding pleasure ([Encyclopedia Britannica https://www.britannica.com/topic/The-Protestant-Ethic-and-the-Spirit- of-Capitalism])

Weber writes, "This ethic was the 'spark' of modern capitalism, but once established, capitalism no longer needs religious support. In other words, even as "Christ (the story of salvation)" weakens, the mechanical economic order remains, and the "obligation" to vocation wanders around like "the ghost of a dead religion. ([gpde.direito.ufmg.br https://gpde.direito.ufmg.br/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/MAX-WEBER.pdf])
→ This is directly related to the "tower is still standing even if the center is removed" feeling of the tweet.
2) "Acting as if one has authority without authority" = internalized "duty of vocation" and secularized capitalist mentality
The second tweet, "Act like you have authority except you are a lunatic," is Weberian,
Even if religion does not directly command it, diligence, temperance, and efficiency are internalized as "good/natural" ([Encyclopedia Britannica https://www.britannica.com/money/Protestant-ethic])

The "spirit" is even "purified" in documents not directly related to religion (e.g. Benjamin Franklin's "time is money") ([gpde.direito.ufmg .br https://gpde.direito.ufmg.br/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/MAX-WEBER.pdf])
It is easier to see that "authority" here is replaced by the norm of vocation = duty (+ the trust, credibility, and discipline it creates), rather than the theology itself.
3) "Is it really holding? Weber's "iron cage" and future uncertainty
The third question, in fact, is also left with an eeriness that is close to Weber's own.

He says that the Puritans worked "voluntarily" in their vocation, while moderns work "under compulsion" in an "iron cage," and leaves the future uncertain: "[A] new prophet, [the rebirth of old ideas], or [mechanized rigidity]..." He also says that the Puritans "worked voluntarily" in their vocation, while moderns work "under compulsion" in an "iron cage. or [mechanized rigidity]..." He leaves the future uncertain. ([gpde.direito.ufmg.br https://gpde.direito.ufmg.br/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/MAX-WEBER.pdf])
So I'd summarize the tweet sequence with Weber,
Short term: weaken the justification (Christ/authority), but the type of conduct (vocation ethics, discipline, institutions) will still turn
Long-term: However, rather than "stability," it could be headed either toward an "iron cage" in which the meaning is stripped away or toward a reorganization into a different philosophy.
...is a point of contention.
3) "Structure is maintained even when authority is removed. People act as if they have authority."
This is the core of the second tweet, and the mechanism can be broken down rather well.
Equilibrium of cooperation:
As long as everyone "treats it as if it were there," it functions the same as if it were there (money, title, company rules, education, etc.).
Internalization:
Discipline yourself without a monitor ("that's the way it is" and "it's a loss if you go against it").
Inertia/cost:
Changing it is tedious and risky, so inertia is maintained.
Substitution for alternative justification:
If God's authority is weakened, another authority like "state," "science," "market," "law," or "human rights" may fill the void.
So it is quite possible that "even if you remove the authority, the structure will turn for a while.
4) But is it really maintained? The "just slowly crumbling" problem
The third tweet is a good tweak, and this is the most important side effect of the Jenga metaphor.
Jenga is not a choice between immediate collapse or eternal stability,
It looks like it is standing, but there is a state where "margin" is decreasing.
Society, too, when legitimacy exits.
Increased policing, monitoring, and accountability costs
Increased dissatisfaction and deviance
Start looking for alternative justifications (another narrative)
It is easy to enter the "maintainable but expensive" phase like
So the conclusion is "sometimes they keep it in the short term / sometimes they reorganize it into another form in the long term" and the tweet "I don't know about that" is rather sincere.
To take this metaphor one step further in precision, the question is probably this:
What we thought was the "center" was actually not a load-bearing component but a "decoration" (a sign to justify)?
Or does it just appear to be standing now, but the internal stresses are increasing and the critical point is near?

pages.title: Military exercises by China at the end of 2025

lines.text: Military exercises by China at the end of 2025
[GPT5.icon]
China's (People's Liberation Army: PLA) military activities that stood out at the end of 2025 (late December - 31 December 2025) were mainly large-scale exercises around Taiwan.
1) What happened (summary)

The Chinese military (mainly in the Eastern War Zone) conducted "Justice Mission 2025," a large-scale exercise surrounding Taiwan (started 12/29 - announced "completion" on 12/31). ([AP News https://apnews.com/article/220fe1000ae4b8c33c0050ff68aa38dc?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

As objectives, the Chinese side emphasized warnings against "Taiwan independence" and "intervention by outside forces. ([Telegraph NEWS https://news.tv-asahi.co.jp/news_international/articles/000475879.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2) Content of the exercise (scope of press base)

Emphasis is placed on movements that anticipate a siege/blockade (on-site inspection, blockade of maritime traffic), and drills in which naval vessels and aircraft approach Taiwan from multiple directions and an integrated (land, sea, air + rocket forces, etc.) immediate response is appealed. ([Teletext NEWS https://news.tv-asahi.co.jp/news_international/articles/000475879.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Live fire (long-range firepower, rockets, etc.) was reported, and Taiwan's announcement stated that 27 rockets, some of which fell within Taiwan's "connecting waters (24 nautical miles)," were positioned as "the closest live ammunition. ([Focus Taiwan - CNA English News https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202512300025?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

As a sense of scale, the Taiwanese side announced (in press) that in one 24-hour period, 77 aircraft and 25 naval vessels, 35 of which crossed the median line of the Taiwan Strait. ([Reuters https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-stays-high-alert-chinese-ships-pull-back-after-massive-drills-2025-12-31/?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])
3) Movements in the immediate vicinity (in the context of "year-end")

In early December, there were reports that over 90 (sometimes over 100) vessels were active not only around Taiwan but also in the Yellow Sea, East China Sea, South China Sea, and West Pacific Ocean, and the "maritime force demonstration" attracted attention as a preliminary step to the year-end exercise. ([Reuters Japan https://jp.reuters.com/world/taiwan/EA65MK4H5NN2LJC62VBSTJIPMQ-2025-12-04/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4) Reactions from various countries (concentrated at the end of the year)

Japan (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) expressed concern, saying that it would increase tensions in the Taiwan Strait. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/press/danwa/pageit_000001_00039.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

France, Germany, and the UK expressed concern (peaceful stability of the Taiwan Strait and opposition to unilateral [status quo] changes). ([Reuters Japan https://jp.reuters.com/world/taiwan/3LQUFTUDTZMTLNSWXM56HHDJFI-2025-12-30/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Australia (DFAT) also noted "serious concerns/ destabilization" and the risk of accidents and miscalculations. ([Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade https://www.dfat.gov.au/news/news/statement-late-december-2025-large-scale-pla-exercises-around-taiwan?utm_source=chatgpt .com])
5) A quick look (discussion point)

The importance of the year-end exercise is that it is not only a demonstration, but also a "demonstration" of a blockade (quasi-blockade). ([Wall Street Journal https://www.wsj.com/world/asia/five-takeaways-from-chinas-military-drills-around-taiwan-47c64aee?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

The trigger is reportedly tied to a backlash against the sale of arms to Taiwan (by the U.S.), among other things. ([Reuters https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-stays-high-alert-chinese-ships-pull-back-after-massive-drills-2025-12-31/?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])
