pages.title: Why Russia considers Ukraine part of itself.

lines.text: Why Russia considers Ukraine part of itself.
Why [Russia] considers [Ukraine] a part of itself
[GPT5.icon]

Broadly speaking, "justification" in terms of Russia's domestic historical perspective and political ideology and "justification under international law" are two different things. In conclusion, there is almost no justification under international law for saying that "Ukraine belongs to Russia. On the other hand, there are some logics (inward justification stories) that Russia likes to think so.
1) The "justification story" that the Russian side tends to claim
A. Unity of history/ethnicity ("same people/same history")

Putin has strongly suggested that Russians and Ukrainians are "one people" and that the modern Ukrainian state was created by outside forces as an "anti-Russian" state. ([Kremlin https://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/66181?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In this framework, the sense that Ukraine is essentially part of the Russian world (Русский мир) and that its separation is unnatural seems "justified".
B. The "coincidence" of the border (it was just an administrative division of the Soviet Union)

The claim that "the current borders are merely administrative lines from the Soviet period / arbitrarily cut by the [Bolsheviks]" can also be used to reinforce A (arguments such as [the transfer of Crimea] also fall here). ([Kremlin https://en.kremlin.ru/events/president/news/66181?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
C. The "Protection of [Russian Speakers]/[Compatriots]" Theory

The logic of "Russian speakers (compatriots) in Ukraine are being persecuted, so we will protect them" (especially since 2014). This kind of logic is easy to sound for domestic purposes (but is a hurdle in international law).
D. Security (NATO Enlargement = Survival Threat) Theory
The geopolitical "necessity" of having Ukraine on its own side as a buffer zone against NATO. This is a "sphere of influence" concept, not "ownership," but it is often mixed up with other concepts.
2) But hardly "legitimate" under international law (rather the opposite)
A. Acquisition of territory by force is prohibited in principle

The [UN Charter] prohibits the use of force (threat or use of force) against the territorial integrity and political independence of other states. ([UN https://www.un.org/en/about-us/un-charter/full-text?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
B. Principle of inviolability of borders and territorial integrity (European security order)

The [Helsinki Final Protocol] (OSCE/CSCE) also focuses on territorial integrity and non-use of force. ([CSCE https://www.csce.gov/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/Helsinki-Final-Act.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
C. Russia itself has confirmed "Ukraine's independence and borders

A representative example is the [Budapest Memorandum], in which Russia reaffirms Ukraine's independence, sovereignty, respect for existing borders, etc. ([World and Japan https://worldjpn.net/documents/texts/mt/19941215.O1E.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

It is also organized that the 1997 "[Treaty of Friendship and Cooperation Partnership]" (the so-called "Big Treaty") clearly states the inviolability of existing borders and respect for territorial integrity. ([Opinio Juris https://opiniojuris.org/2019/05/01/termination-of-the-treaty-of-friendship-between-ukraine-and-russia-too-little-too- late-%EF%BB%BF/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
D. [UN General Assembly] rejects "invasion" and "annexation".

The UN General Assembly resolution reaffirms Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity by characterizing Russia's actions as "aggression". ([UN document https://docs.un.org/en/A/RES/ES-11/1?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
E. [International Court of Justice] (ICJ) also ordered suspension (provisional measures)
In March 2022, the ICJ (albeit with a different argument) issued interim measures ordering Russia to cease military action. ([ICJ https://www.icj-cij.org/node/106135?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3) How to organize "legitimacy" to make it easier to understand
"Kinship" as an emotional and historical view (syncretism, imperial history, religious and cultural spheres, etc.)
→ Can be used for domestic political mobilization, but not for territorial title (ownership).
Security Convenience (sphere of influence, buffer zone)
→ It is spoken of as a reality of international politics, but not as a basis for erasing the sovereignty of other countries.
Legitimacy under International Law
→ In principle, "Ukraine belongs to Ukraine" and changes require very limited procedures such as agreement of the parties.

lines.text: Why China considers Taiwan part of itself.
[GPT5.icon]
What is the "legitimacy" of the claim that Taiwan is "theirs" in the eyes of China ([PRC])?
(1) Justification within China's domestic historical and legal system and,
(2) Legitimacy that is applicable in international law and international politics
It is easier to organize if you separate the
1) Logic that the Chinese side considers "legitimate" (justification for domestic use)

The "[One China]" principle: Taiwan is an inseparable part of China, and unification is an "internal affair," a position repeated in official documents. ([State Council of the People's Republic of China https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/whitepaper/202208/10/content_WS62f34f46c6d02e533532f0ac.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com ])

Narrative of history and postwar handling: The explanation that "Taiwan, which Japan took, should have returned (returned) to China" is put forward on the basis of the Cairo Declaration, Potsdam Declaration, and other documents. ([中国驻伊朗大使馆 https://ir.china-embassy.gov.cn/eng/fyrth/202512/t20251216_11774382.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Domestic Legal Status: The 2005 "Anti-Divisive State Law" is against "divisiveness" in Taiwan and provides the appearance of a "legal basis" domestically, with the structure that "non-peaceful measures" may be taken in certain cases ([European Parliament, ]). ([European Parliament https://www.europarl.europa.eu/meetdocs/2004_2009/documents/fd/d-cn2005042601/d-cn2005042601en.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In short, the three-stage argument that "historically belonged to China," "the postwar order confirmed this," and "therefore unification is a domestic issue" is the Chinese justification story.
2) However, in international law and politics, "ownership" is highly contested.

Principle of not changing the status quo by force: The UN Charter prohibits the threat or use of force and states that disputes should be resolved by peaceful means. Even if there is a claim, it is difficult to justify the use of force to achieve "possession". ([UN https://www.un.org/en/about-us/un-charter/full-text?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The way the Treaty of Peace with Japan ([San Francisco Peace Treaty]) is written: It clearly states that Japan "renounced all right, title and claim" to Taiwan (Formosa) and Penghu, but does not specify in the treaty "to whom they shall belong," which has been a source of legal controversy. This has become a source of legal debate. ([United Nations Treaties https://treaties.un.org/doc/publication/unts/volume%20136/volume-136-i-1832-english.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The scope of [UN General Assembly Resolution 2758]: There is a strong interpretation, at least in part, that this resolution deals with who has the "right to represent China" (recognizing the PRC as the representative of China and expelling the [Chiang Kai-shek] representative) and does not determine the ownership of Taiwan's sovereignty itself. The U.S. Supreme Court has not yet decided on the issue. ([U.S.-Asia Law Institute https://usali.org/publications/talking-points-what-does-the-united-nations-say-about-taiwan?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

Typical of the position of major countries (U.S.): It is repeatedly explained that the U.S. "acknowledges" the Chinese position with its "one China policy," but does not determine its own position on Taiwan's sovereignty. ([Congress.gov https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF10275?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Effective Rule (Reality): Although the PRC claims Taiwan as "its own territory," it is clearly stated by the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and others that the PRC has never governed Taiwan. ([Congress.gov https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IF10275?utm_source=chatgpt.com]) Also, Taiwan has its own government, military, currency, passports, etc., and is effectively governed independently. ([Reuters https://www.reuters.com/world/china/what-is-taiwan-independence-is-taiwan-already-independent-2025-12-30/?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Summary: To what extent is it "legitimate"?

The logic of considering "our own" is constructed in the Chinese domestic narrative and domestic law. ([State Council of the People's Republic of China https://english.www.gov.cn/archive/whitepaper/202208/10/content_WS62f34f46c6d02e533532f0ac.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com ])

There is a great deal of conflict in the sense that "ownership is fixed" under international law, and at the very least, "unification by force" is in strong tension with the principles of the UN Charter. ([UN https://www.un.org/en/about-us/un-charter/full-text?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

The interpretation of postwar documents (Cairo, Potsdam, etc.) also continues to be an antagonistic structure, with China using it as a basis, and the U.S. and other countries refuting it, saying that it has not established its political status. ([Reuters https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-says-china-spreads-false-world-war-two-narratives-pressure-taiwan-2025-09-15/?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])

"Family" is a group. Not all members of a family have common features. Even if there are no common features to all members, partially common features loosely connect members to form a group.

The word "family resemblance" was made by [Ludwig Wittgenstein]. He wondered if what was called a "game" had common features. He concluded that there is not a feature that is common to all games, but there is a mesh of complex similarities that overlap each other. He called the group connected by family resemblance "family."

In classification, we determine "features common to groups" ([criteria]) in advance, and determines whether a piece is a member of the group based on the presence or absence of the features. On the other hand, in [group organization] of the KJ method, we focus there is a relationship between individual members and does not require common features. The concept of group organization is very similar to the concept of family resemblance.
You do not need to create a group with common features.

(*1): Norenzayan, A., Smith, E. E., Kim, B. J., & Nisbett, R. E. (2002). [Cultural preferences for formal versus intuitive reasoning]. Cognitive science, 26(5), 653-684.

Rule-based: Features 1 to 3 do not clearly separate groups. Feature 4 is the criteria to separate these two groups. The target has a straight stem. So it is similar to group 2.
Family resemblance-based: Features 1 to 3 say the target is more similar to group 1 than group 2. The 3 out of 4 features indicate that it is similar to group 1. So it is similar to group 1.

Sum the number of votes to determine the group with the highest number.

pages.title: Good ideas solve multiple problems at once.

lines.text: Good ideas solve multiple problems at once.
[GPT5.icon]

A good idea solves multiple problems at once" / "[An idea is something that solves multiple problems at once]" is widely quoted as a statement by [Shigeru Miyamoto] (Shigeru Miyamoto) of [Nintendo]. In Nintendo's official "Iwata Asks," Miyamoto is quoted as saying, "[An idea is a single solution that solves multiple issues at once. (= Solving multiple problems at once with a single solution). ([Nintendo Co., Ltd. https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Iwata-Asks/Iwata-Asks-New-Super-Luigi-U/New-Super-Luigi-U/3-Nabbit-Solves- Multiple-Issues-at-Once/3-Nabbit-Solves-Multiple-Issues-at-Once-786913.html?srsltid=AfmBOoprftcGoB7_wz329c2pxKzOofWA4fmaA4iZdepp6 Fem4Gb6SWhD])
What it means (Explanation)
The point of this phrase is to distinguish "ideas" from "symptomatic devices."
Symptomatic treatment: Problem A appears → destroy only A. Next, problem B appears → destroy only B.
(As a result, the mechanism tends to be patchy.)
Idea:
When you look closely at problems A, B, and C, they all come from the "same root.
Make one move that works for the root (structure) and multiple problems disappear all together.

In other words, a "good idea" is defined as "one that simultaneously unravels multiple constraints and frustrations with a single change or shift in thinking. ([Nintendo Co., Ltd. https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Iwata-Asks/Iwata-Asks-New-Super-Luigi-U/New-Super-Luigi-U/3-Nabbit-Solves- Multiple-Issues-at-Once/3-Nabbit-Solves-Multiple-Issues-at-Once-786913.html?srsltid=AfmBOoprftcGoB7_wz329c2pxKzOofWA4fmaA4iZdepp6 Fem4Gb6SWhD])
Example (in the context of Nintendo)
The Nintendo interview applies this very concept to "game specifications".

For example, "Mario can now jump" is not just about more controls, but also about solving multiple problems at the same time (such as playability, terrain design, and visual appeal) (the purpose of "jumps have made it possible to solve multiple problems at the same time"). (The purpose of "jump" is "to solve multiple problems at the same time"). ([Nintendo Co., Ltd. https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Iwata-Asks/Iwata-Asks-New-Super-Mario-Bros-Wii/Volume-1/1-Mario-Couldn-t-Jump-At- First/1-Mario-Couldn't-Jump-At-First-210699.html?srsltid=AfmBOoo7gHbSo24evsYnuxpM78lLSuyfiF8Y8TeM2ZY73MnDY_X1U3A1])

In another "The President Asks," Miyamoto's definition of "idea = solving multiple problems in one move" is drawn as a footnote in the flow of the article, in which he says that by adding certain new elements (e.g., relief for beginners, easier explanation of play, etc.), multiple issues can be solved at once. ([Nintendo Co., Ltd. https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Iwata-Asks/Iwata-Asks-New-Super-Luigi-U/New-Super-Luigi-U/3-Nabbit-Solves- Multiple-Issues-at-Once/3-Nabbit-Solves-Multiple-Issues-at-Once-786913.html?srsltid=AfmBOoprftcGoB7_wz329c2pxKzOofWA4fmaA4iZdepp6 Fem4Gb6SWhD])
I'll take it one step further.

What is interesting is that Mr. Miyamoto himself stated, "After Mr. Iwata spread the idea, I began to think that it was indeed true. ([Nintendo Co., Ltd. https://www.nintendo.com/en-gb/Iwata-Asks/Super-Mario-Bros-25th-Anniversary/Vol-1-Itoi-asks-Miyamoto/2-You-re- Pretty-Negative-2-You-re-Pretty-Negative--217256.html?srsltid=AfmBOopi9lD5iA0u8n1tKDilYGQzHoeN3u80KF-90vDBWB6759XrrKKp])
(This phenomenon is called "the circulation of language helps to organize the person's thoughts").
Tips on how to put this into practice (make this language into a usable form)
If you want to use this word without ending up with "aphorisms," it is easier to get into the order of ideas like this.
1. list the problems (A/B/C...)
